1.1: And there was a certain man of Ramathayim Tsophim, of the mountains of Ephrayim, and his name was Elqanah son of Yeroḥam, son of Elihu, son of Toḥu, son of Tsuph, an Ephrayimite.
1.2: And he had two wives, the name of one was Ḥannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Ḥannah had no children.
1.3: Now this man went up from his city year by year to worship and to slaughter to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Ĕli, Ḥophni and Pineḥas, the kohenim of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, were there.
1.4: And when the day came for Elqanah to make an offering, he gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and daughters,
1.5: but, although he loved Ḥannah, he gave only one portion to Ḥannah, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had shut up her womb.
1.6: Moreover, her rival also provoked her greatly, to make her irritable, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had shut up her womb.
1.7: And so he did, year by year. Whenever she went up to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, she was provoked, so that she wept and did not eat.
1.8: And her husband Elqanah said to her, “Ḥannah, why do you weep? Why do you not eat? And why is your heart sad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”
1.9: And Ḥannah rose up after eating and drinking in Shiloh, while Ĕli the kohĕn was sitting on the seat by the doorpost of the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.10: And she was bitter in life, and prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and wept greatly.
1.11: And she made a vow and said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, if You would indeed look on the affliction of your female servant and remember me, and not forget your female servant, but shall give your female servant a male child, then I shall give him to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 all the days of his life, and let no razor come upon his head.”
1.12: And it came to be, as she kept on praying before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that Ĕli was watching her mouth.
1.13: And Ḥannah spoke in her heart, only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. So Ĕli thought she was drunk.
1.14: Then Ĕli said to her, “How long are you going to be drunk? Put your wine away from you!”
1.15: And Ḥannah answered and said, “No, my master, I am a woman pained in spirit. And I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my being before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.16: “Do not take your female servant for a daughter of Beliya’al, for it is out of my great concern and provocation that I have spoken until now.”
1.17: And Ĕli answered and said, “Go in peace, and the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl give you your petition which you have asked of Him.”
1.18: And she said, “Let your female servant find favor in your eyes.” And the woman went her way and ate, and her face was no more sad.
1.19: And they rose up early in the morning and worshipped before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and returned and came to their house at Ramah. And Elqanah knew Ḥannah his wife, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 remembered her.
1.20: And it came to be at the turn of days, that Ḥannah conceived and bore a son, and called his name Shemu’ĕl, “Because I have asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for him.”
1.21: And the man Elqanah and all his house went up to offer to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the yearly slaughtering and his vow.
1.22: But Ḥannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, “When the child is weaned, then I shall take him. And he shall appear before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and remain forever there.”
1.23: And her husband Elqanah said to her, “Do what is good in your eyes. Remain until you have weaned him. Only let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 establish His word.” And the woman remained and nursed her son until she had weaned him.
1.24: And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with a three year old bull, and one ĕphah of flour, and a skin of wine, and brought him to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in Shiloh. And the child was young.
1.25: And they slaughtered a bull, and brought the child to Ĕli.
1.26: And she said, “O my master! As your being lives, my master, I am the woman who stood by you here, praying to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.27: “I prayed for this youth, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has granted me what I asked of Him.
1.28: “So I have also loaned him to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. All the days that he lives he shall be loaned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” And he worshipped there before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

10.1: And Shemu’ĕl took a flask of oil and poured it on his head, and kissed him and said, “Is it not because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has anointed you leader over His inheritance?
10.2: “When you leave me today, you shall find two men by Raḥĕl’s tomb in the border of Binyamin at Tseltsaḥ, and they shall say to you, ‘The donkeys which you went to look for have been found. And see, your father has left the matters of the donkeys and is worrying about you, saying, “What shall I do for my son?” ’
10.3: “And you shall pass on from there, and beyond, and shall come to the terebinth tree of Taḇor. And three men going up to Elohim at Bĕyth Ĕl shall find you there, one bearing three young goats, another bearing three loaves of bread, and another bearing a skin of wine.
10.4: “And they shall greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you shall accept from their hand.
10.5: “After that go to the hill of Elohim where the Pelishtite watch-post is. And it shall be, when you have come there to the city, that you shall meet a group of neḇi’im coming down from the high place with a stringed instrument, and a tambourine, and a flute, and a lyre before them, and they naḇa.
10.6: “And the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall come upon you, and you shall naḇa with them and be turned into another man.
10.7: “And it shall be, when these signs come to you, do for yourself as your hand finds to do, for Elohim is with you.
10.8: “And you shall go down before me to Gilgal. And see, I am coming down to you to slaughter burnt offerings and make peace offerings. Wait seven days, till I come to you, then I shall make known to you what you should do.”
10.9: And it came to be, when he had turned his back to go from Shemu’ĕl, that Elohim gave him another heart. And all those signs came on that day.
10.10: And they came there to the hill and saw a group of neḇi’im, to meet him. And the Ruaḥ of Elohim came upon him, and he naḇu in their midst.
10.11: And it came to be, all who knew him formerly looked and saw that he naḇu among the neḇi’im. So the people said to each other, “What is this that has come upon the son of Qish? Is Sha’ul also among the neḇi’im?”
10.12: And a man there answered and said, “And who is their father?” That is why it became a proverb, “Is Sha’ul also among the neḇi’im?”
10.13: And when he stopped naḇa, he went to the high place.
10.14: And the uncle of Sha’ul asked him and his servant, “Where did you go?” And he said, “To look for the donkeys. And when we saw that they were nowhere to be found, we went to Shemu’ĕl.”
10.15: And the uncle of Sha’ul said, “Please inform me what Shemu’ĕl said to you.”
10.16: And Sha’ul said to his uncle, “He informed us plainly that the donkeys had been found.” But he did not disclose to him about the matter of the reign, what Shemu’ĕl had said.
10.17: And Shemu’ĕl called the people together to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Mitspah,
10.18: and said to the children of Yisra’ĕl, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘I have brought Yisra’ĕl up out of Mitsrayim, and delivered you from the hand of the Mitsrites and from the hand of all reigns and from those who oppressed you.’
10.19: “And today you have rejected your Elohim, who Himself saved you out of all your evils and your distresses. And you have said to Him, ‘No, but appoint a meleḵ over us!’ And now, present yourselves before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by your tribes and by your clans.”
10.20: And Shemu’ĕl brought near all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, and the tribe of Binyamin was taken.
10.21: Then he brought near the tribe of Binyamin, by their clans, and the clan of Matri was taken, and Sha’ul son of Qish was taken. And when they sought him, he could not be found.
10.22: And they asked again of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Has the man come here yet?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 answered, “See, he has hidden by the baggage.”
10.23: And they ran and brought him from there. And he stood in the midst of the people, and he was taller than any of the people, from his shoulders and upwards.
10.24: And Shemu’ĕl said to all the people, “Do you see him whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has chosen, that there is no one like him among all the people?” And all the people shouted and said, “Let the meleḵ live!”
10.25: And Shemu’ĕl declared to the people the rulings of the reign, and wrote it in a book and placed it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And Shemu’ĕl sent all the people away, each to his house.
10.26: And Sha’ul went to his house too, to Giḇ’ah. And with him went brave men whose hearts Elohim had touched.
10.27: But the sons of Beliya’al said, “What! Does this one save us?” And they despised him, and brought him no presents. But he kept silent.

11.1: And Naḥash the Ammonite came up and camped against Yaḇĕsh Gil’aḏ. And all the men of Yaḇĕsh said to Naḥash, “Make a covenant with us, and we shall serve you.”
11.2: Then Naḥash the Ammonite answered them, “For this I make a covenant with you, that I dig out all your right eyes, and I shall bring reproach on all Yisra’ĕl.”
11.3: And the elders of Yaḇĕsh said to him, “Leave us alone for seven days, so that we send messengers to all the borders of Yisra’ĕl. And then, if there is no one to save us, we shall come out to you.”
11.4: And the messengers came to Giḇ’ah of Sha’ul and spoke the words in the hearing of the people. And all the people lifted up their voices and wept.
11.5: And look, Sha’ul was coming behind the herd from the field. And Sha’ul said, “Why are the people weeping?” And they related to him the words of the men of Yaḇĕsh.
11.6: And the Ruaḥ of Elohim came upon Sha’ul mightily as he heard these words, and his displeasure burned greatly.
11.7: And he took a yoke of cattle and cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the border of Yisra’ĕl by the hands of messengers, saying, “Whoever does not go out with Sha’ul and Shemu’ĕl to battle, let this be done to his cattle.” And the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fell on the people, and they came out as one man.
11.8: And he mustered them in Bezeq, and the children of Yisra’ĕl were three hundred thousand, and the men of Yahuḏah thirty thousand.
11.9: And they said to the messengers who came, “Say this to the men of Yaḇĕsh Gil’aḏ, ‘Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you shall have help.’ ” Then the messengers came and informed the men of Yaḇĕsh, and they rejoiced.
11.10: So the men of Yaḇĕsh said, “Tomorrow we come out to you, and you shall do to us whatever seems good to you.”
11.11: And it came to be, on the next day, that Sha’ul put the people in three companies. And they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch and smote Ammon until the heat of the day. And it came to be that those left were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
11.12: And the people said to Shemu’ĕl, “Who said, ‘Shall Sha’ul reign over us?’ Bring the men, so that we put them to death.”
11.13: But Sha’ul said, “No man is put to death this day, for today 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has wrought deliverance in Yisra’ĕl.”
11.14: And Shemu’ĕl said to the people, “Come, and let us go to Gilgal and renew the reign there.”
11.15: And all the people went to Gilgal, and there they appointed Sha’ul to reign before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in Gilgal, and there they made slaughterings of peace offerings before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And there Sha’ul rejoiced, and all the men of Yisra’ĕl, very greatly.

12.1: And Shemu’ĕl said to all Yisra’ĕl, “Look, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and have appointed a meleḵ over you.
12.2: “And now, look, the meleḵ is walking before you. And I am old and grey, and look, my sons are with you. And I have walked before you from my youth to this day.
12.3: “Look, here I am. Witness against me before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and before His anointed: Whose ox have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken, or whom have I oppressed? Whom have I abused, or from whose hand have I received any bribe with which to blind my eyes? - then I restore it to you.”
12.4: And they said, “You have not oppressed us or abused us, nor have you taken any from anyone’s hand.”
12.5: So he said to them, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is witness against you, and His anointed is witness today, that you have found naught in my hand.” And they answered, “He is witness.”
12.6: And Shemu’ĕl said to the people, “It is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who appointed Mosheh and Aharon, and who brought your fathers up from the land of Mitsrayim.
12.7: “And now, stand still, so that I judge you before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 concerning all the righteous acts of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He did to you and your fathers:
12.8: “When Ya’aqoḇ had come to Mitsrayim, and your fathers cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent Mosheh and Aharon, who brought your fathers out of Mitsrayim and made them dwell in this place.
12.9: “But they forgot 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim, so He sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Ḥatsor, and into the hand of the Pelishtites, and into the hand of the meleḵ of Mo’aḇ. And they fought against them.
12.10: “And they cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and said, ‘We have sinned, because we have forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and served the Ba’als and the Ashtaroth. And now, deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we serve You.’
12.11: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent Yerubba’al, and Beḏan, and Yiphtaḥ, and Shemu’ĕl, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies round about, and you dwelt in safety.
12.12: “And when you saw that Naḥash meleḵ of the children of Ammon came against you, you said to me, ‘No, but let a meleḵ reign over us,’ when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim was your meleḵ.
12.13: “And now, here is the meleḵ whom you have chosen and whom you have asked. And see, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has appointed a meleḵ over you.
12.14: “If you revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and shall serve Him and obey His voice, and not rebel against the Command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, then both you and the meleḵ who reigns over you shall follow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
12.15: “But if you do not obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and shall rebel against the Command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, then the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall be against you, as it was against your fathers.
12.16: “And now, stand and see this great matter which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 does before your eyes:
12.17: “Is today not the wheat harvest? Let me call to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, so that He sends thunder and rain - know then and see that your evil is great, which you have done in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in asking for yourselves a meleḵ.”
12.18: And Shemu’ĕl called to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent thunder and rain that day. And all the people greatly revered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and Shemu’ĕl.
12.19: And all the people said to Shemu’ĕl, “Pray for your servants to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, that we do not die, for we have added to all our sins by doing evil in asking for ourselves a meleḵ.”
12.20: And Shemu’ĕl said to the people, “Do not fear. You have done all this evil. Only, do not turn aside from following 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And you shall serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with all your heart,
12.21: and do not turn aside after worthlessness which does not profit or deliver, for they are worthless.
12.22: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 would not cast away His people, for His great Name’s sake, seeing it has pleased 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to make you His people.
12.23: “Also, as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in ceasing to pray for you, but I shall teach you the good and straight Way.
12.24: “Only revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and you shall serve Him in truth with all your heart, for consider what marvels He has done for you.
12.25: “But if you persist in doing evil, both you and your meleḵ are consumed.”

13.1: Sha’ul was . . . years old when he began to reign. And when he had reigned two years over Yisra’ĕl,
13.2: Sha’ul chose for himself three thousand men of Yisra’ĕl. And two thousand were with Sha’ul in Miḵmash and in the mountains of Bĕyth Ĕl, and a thousand were with Yahonathan in Giḇ’ah of Binyamin. And the rest of the people he sent away, each to his tent.
13.3: And Yahonathan smote the watch-post of the Pelishtites that was in Geḇa, and the Pelishtites heard of it. And Sha’ul blew the ram’s horn throughout all the land, saying, “Let the Iḇrim hear!”
13.4: And all Yisra’ĕl heard the news that Sha’ul had smitten a watch-post of the Pelishtites, and also that Yisra’ĕl had become a stench to the Pelishtites. And the people were summoned to Sha’ul at Gilgal.
13.5: And the Pelishtites gathered to fight Yisra’ĕl, thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and people as numerous as the sand on the seashore. And they came up and camped in Miḵmash, east of Bĕyth Awen.
13.6: And the men of Yisra’ĕl saw that they were in trouble, for the people were distressed, and the people hid in caves, and in thorny bushes, and in rocks, and in holes, and in pits.
13.7: And Iḇrim passed over the Yardĕn to the land of Gaḏ and Gil’aḏ. But Sha’ul was still in Gilgal, and all the people followed him, trembling.
13.8: And he waited for seven days, according to the appointment with Shemu’ĕl. But Shemu’ĕl did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattered from him.
13.9: And Sha’ul said, “Bring a burnt offering and peace offerings here to me.” And he offered the burnt offering.
13.10: And it came to be, as he had finished offering the burnt offering, look, Shemu’ĕl came. And Sha’ul went out to meet him, to baraḵ him.
13.11: Then Shemu’ĕl said, “What have you done?” And Sha’ul said, “Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that you did not come within the days appointed, and that the Pelishtites gathered at Miḵmash,
13.12: so I said, ‘The Pelishtites are going to come down on me at Gilgal, and I have not appeased the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’ So I felt compelled, and offered a burnt offering.”
13.13: And Shemu’ĕl said to Sha’ul, “You have been foolish. You have not guarded the Command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, which He commanded you. For now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 would have established your reign over Yisra’ĕl forever.
13.14: “But now, your reign is not going to stand. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall seek for Himself a man after His own heart, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall command him to be leader over His people, because you have not guarded what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded you.”
13.15: And Shemu’ĕl arose and went up from Gilgal to Giḇ’ah of Binyamin. And Sha’ul mustered the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.
13.16: And Sha’ul, and Yahonathan his son, and the people who were present with them remained in Giḇ’ah of Binyamin, while the Pelishtites camped at Miḵmash.
13.17: And from the camp of the Pelishtites raiders went out in three companies. The one company turned to the way that leads to Ophrah, to the land of Shu’al,
13.18: and another company turned toward the way of Bĕyth Ḥoron, and another company turned toward the way of the border that overlooks the Valley of Tseḇo’im toward the wilderness.
13.19: Now no blacksmith could be found in all the land of Yisra’ĕl, for the Pelishtites said, “Lest the Iḇrim make swords or spears.”
13.20: And all Yisra’ĕl went down to the Pelishtites, each one to sharpen his ploughshare, and his mattock, and his axe, and his sickle.
13.21: And the charge was a pim for the ploughshares, and the mattocks, and the forks, and the axes, and to appoint the goads.
13.22: And it came to be, on the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people who were with Sha’ul and Yahonathan. But they were found with Sha’ul and Yahonathan his son.
13.23: And the outpost of the Pelishtites went out to the pass of Miḵmash.

14.1: And it came to be one day that Yahonathan son of Sha’ul said to the young man who bore his armor, “Come, and let us go over to the outpost of the Pelishtites which is on the other side.” But he did not inform his father.
14.2: And Sha’ul remained at the outskirts of Giḇ’ah under a pomegranate tree at Miḡron, and the people who were with him were about six hundred men.
14.3: And Aḥiyahu son of Aḥituḇ, Iḵaḇoḏ’s brother, son of Pineḥas, son of Ĕli, the kohĕn of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in Shiloh, was wearing a shoulder garment. And the people did not know that Yahonathan had gone.
14.4: And between the passes, by which Yahonathan sought to go over to the outpost of the Pelishtites, there was an edge of a rock on one side and an edge of a rock on the other side. And the name, of one was Botsĕts, and the name of the other Seneh.
14.5: The one edge was on the north opposite Miḵmash, and the other on the south opposite Giḇ’ah.
14.6: And Yahonathan said to the young man who bore his armor, “Come, and let us go over to the outpost of these uncircumcised. If so be, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 works for us. For there is no hindrance for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 save by many or by few.”
14.7: And his armor-bearer said to him, “Do all that is in your heart, incline yourself. See, I am with you, according to your heart.”
14.8: And Yahonathan said, “See, we are passing over to the men - and show ourselves to them.
14.9: “If they say this to us, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ then we shall stand still in our place and not go up to them.
14.10: “But if they say this, ‘Come up to us,’ then we shall go up. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given them into our hand, and this is the sign to us.”
14.11: And both them disclosed themselves to the outpost of the Pelishtites, and the Pelishtites said, “See, the Iḇrim are coming out of the holes where they have hidden.”
14.12: And the men of the outpost called to Yahonathan and his armor-bearer, and said, “Come up to us, and let us teach you a lesson.” Then Yahonathan said to his armor-bearer, “Come up after me, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given them into the hand of Yisra’ĕl.”
14.13: And Yahonathan climbed up on his hands and knees with his armor-bearer after him. And they fell before Yahonathan, and his armor-bearer was putting them to death behind him.
14.14: And that first slaughter which Yahonathan and his armor-bearer made was about twenty men, in about half a yoke-furrowed field.
14.15: And there was trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. The outpost and the raiders also trembled, and the ground shook. And it became a trembling of Elohim.
14.16: And the watchmen of Sha’ul in Giḇ’ah of Binyamin looked and saw the crowd melting away, and they went here and there.
14.17: And Sha’ul said to the people who were with him, “Please inspect and see who has gone from us.” So they inspected and saw that Yahonathan and his armor-bearer were missing.
14.18: And Sha’ul said to Aḥiyahu, “Bring the ark of Elohim here.” For the ark of Elohim was with the children of Yisra’ĕl on that day.
14.19: And it came to be, while Sha’ul talked to the kohĕn, that the noise which was in the camp of the Pelishtites went on, and became great, so Sha’ul said to the kohĕn, “Withdraw your hand.”
14.20: And Sha’ul was called, and all the people who were with him, and they went to the battle. And see, every man’s sword was against his neighbor - a very great confusion.
14.21: And the Iḇrim who were with the Pelishtites before that time, who went up with them into the camp, turned round, they too, to be with Yisra’ĕl, who were with Sha’ul and Yahonathan.
14.22: And all the men of Yisra’ĕl who had hidden in the mountains of Ephrayim, heard that the Pelishtites fled, and they also pursued them in the battle.
14.23: Thus 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saved Yisra’ĕl that day, and the battle passed over to Bĕyth Awen.
14.24: And the men of Yisra’ĕl were distressed that day, for Sha’ul had placed the people under oath, saying, “Cursed be the man who eats food until evening, and I have taken revenge on my enemies.” Therefore none of the people tasted food.
14.25: And all the land came into the woods, and there was honey on the ground.
14.26: And the people came into the woods and saw the honey, dripping. But no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people revered the oath.
14.27: But Yahonathan had not heard that his father had taken an oath of the people, and he stretched out the end of the rod that was in his hand and dipped it in a honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth. And his eyes lit up.
14.28: Then one of the people said, “Your father strictly took an oath of the people, saying, ‘Cursed be the man who eats food today.’ ” And the people were weary.
14.29: And Yahonathan said, “My father has troubled the land. Now see how my eyes lit up when I tasted a little of this honey.
14.30: “How much better if the people had well eaten today of the spoil of their enemies which they found! For then, would not the smiting among the Pelishtites have been greater?”
14.31: And they smote the Pelishtites that day from Miḵmash to Ayalon. So the people were very weary,
14.32: and the people pounced on the spoil, and took sheep, and cattle, and calves, and slaughtered them on the ground. And the people ate with the blood.
14.33: And they told Sha’ul, saying, “Look, the people are sinning against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by eating with the blood!” And he said, “You have acted treacherously. Roll a large stone to me today.”
14.34: And Sha’ul said, “Disperse among the people, and say to them, ‘Each one bring his ox near to me, and each one his sheep, and you shall slaughter them here, and eat. And do not sin against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by eating with the blood.’ ” So every one of the people brought his ox with him that night, and slaughtered it there.
14.35: And Sha’ul built an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. It was the first altar he built to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
14.36: And Sha’ul said, “Let us go down after the Pelishtites by night, and plunder them until the morning light, and not leave a man of them.” And they said, “Do whatever seems good to you.” But the kohĕn said, “Let us draw near to Elohim here.”
14.37: And Sha’ul asked of Elohim, “Should I go down after the Pelishtites? Do You give them into the hand of Yisra’ĕl?” But He did not answer him that day.
14.38: And Sha’ul said, “Come over here, all you chiefs of the people, and know and see what this sin was today.
14.39: “For as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, who saves Yisra’ĕl, though it be in Yahonathan my son, he shall certainly die.” But not one among all the people answered him.
14.40: And he said to all Yisra’ĕl, “You be on one side, and my son Yahonathan and I be on the other side.” And the people said to Sha’ul, “Do what seems good to you.”
14.41: Then Sha’ul said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “Give a perfect one.” And Sha’ul and Yahonathan were taken, but the people escaped.
14.42: And Sha’ul said, “Cast between my son Yahonathan and me.” And Yahonathan was taken.
14.43: Sha’ul then said to Yahonathan, “Explain to me what you have done.” And Yahonathan explained to him, and said, “I only tasted a little honey with the end of the rod that was in my hand. “See, let me die!”
14.44: And Sha’ul answered, “Elohim do so and more also, for you shall certainly die, Yahonathan.”
14.45: But the people said to Sha’ul, “Should Yahonathan die, who has wrought this great deliverance in Yisra’ĕl? Far be it! As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, let not one hair of his head fall to the ground, for he has wrought with Elohim this day.” Thus the people rescued Yahonathan, and he did not die.
14.46: And Sha’ul returned from pursuing the Pelishtites, and the Pelishtites went to their own place.
14.47: And Sha’ul took the reign over Yisra’ĕl, and fought against all his enemies round about, against Mo’aḇ, and against the children of Ammon, and against Eḏom, and against the melaḵim of Tsoḇah, and against the Pelishtites. And wherever he turned, he caused trouble.
14.48: And he gathered an army and smote the Amalĕqites, and delivered Yisra’ĕl from the hands of those who plundered them.
14.49: And the sons of Sha’ul were Yahonathan and Yishwi and Malkishua. And the names of his two daughters were these: the name of the first-born Mĕraḇ, and the name of the younger Miḵal.
14.50: And the name of Sha’ul’s wife was Aḥino’am the daughter of Aḥima’ats. And the name of the commander of his army was Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, uncle of Sha’ul.
14.51: And Qish was the father of Sha’ul, and Nĕr the father of Aḇnĕr was the son of Aḇi’ĕl.
14.52: And there was fierce fighting against the Pelishtites all the days of Sha’ul. And when Sha’ul saw any mighty man or any brave man, he took him for himself.

15.1: And Shemu’ĕl said to Sha’ul, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent me to anoint you meleḵ over His people, over Yisra’ĕl. And now, listen to the voice of the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.2: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, ‘I shall punish Amalĕq for what he did to Yisra’ĕl, how he positioned against him on the way when he came up from Mitsrayim.
15.3: ‘Now go, and you shall smite Amalĕq and put under the ban all that he has, and you shall not spare them, and put to death from man to woman, from infant to nursing child, from ox to sheep, from camel to donkey.’ ”
15.4: Then Sha’ul summoned the people and mustered them in Tela’im, two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Yahuḏah.
15.5: And Sha’ul came to a city of Amalĕq, and lay in wait in the wadi.
15.6: And Sha’ul said to the Qĕynites, “Go, turn aside, come down from among the Amalĕqites, lest I destroy you with them. For you showed kindness to all the children of Yisra’ĕl when they came up out of Mitsrayim.” So the Qĕynites turned aside from the midst of the Amalĕqites.
15.7: And Sha’ul smote the Amalĕqites, from Ḥawilah all the way to Shur, which is before Mitsrayim.
15.8: And he caught Aḡaḡ meleḵ of the Amalĕqites alive, and put under the ban all the people with the edge of the sword.
15.9: But Sha’ul and the people spared Aḡaḡ and the best of the sheep, and the cattle, and the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not put them under the ban. But all goods despised and worthless, that they put under the ban.
15.10: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Shemu’ĕl, saying,
15.11: “I am grieved that I have appointed Sha’ul as meleḵ, for he has turned back from following Me, and has not performed My Words.” And it displeased Shemu’ĕl, and he cried to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 all night.
15.12: And Shemu’ĕl rose early in the morning to meet Sha’ul, and it was told to Shemu’ĕl, saying, “Sha’ul went to Karmel, and see, he put up a monument for himself, then turned and passed over, and went down to Gilgal.”
15.13: And Shemu’ĕl came to Sha’ul, and Sha’ul said to him, “Baruḵ are you of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄! I have performed the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
15.14: But Shemu’ĕl said, “What then is this bleating of the sheep in my ears, and the lowing of the cattle which I hear?”
15.15: And Sha’ul said, “They have brought them from Amalĕq, because the people spared the best of the sheep and the cattle, to slaughter to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim. And the rest we have put under the ban.”
15.16: And Shemu’ĕl said to Sha’ul, “Wait, and let me declare to you what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me last night.” And he said to him, “Speak.”
15.17: And Shemu’ĕl said, “Though you were little in your own eyes, were you not head of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl? And did not 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 anoint you meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl?
15.18: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent you on the way, and said, ‘Go, and you shall put under the ban the sinners, the Amalĕqites, and fight against them until they are consumed.’
15.19: “And why did you not obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but swooped down on the spoil, and did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?”
15.20: And Sha’ul said to Shemu’ĕl, “I did obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and I went on the way on which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent me, and brought back Aḡaḡ meleḵ of Amalĕq, and I put Amalĕq under the ban.
15.21: “But the people took of the spoil, of the sheep and cattle, the best of that which should have been put under the ban, to slaughter to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim in Gilgal.”
15.22: Then Shemu’ĕl said, “Does 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 delight in burnt offerings and slaughterings, as in obeying the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄? Look, to obey is better than an offering, and to heed than the fat of rams.
15.23: “For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and stubbornness is as wickedness and idolatry. Because you have rejected the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, He also rejects you as meleḵ.”
15.24: And Sha’ul said to Shemu’ĕl, “I have sinned, for I have transgressed the Command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and your words, because I feared the people and listened to their voice.
15.25: “And now, please pardon my sin, and return with me, and let me bow myself to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
15.26: But Shemu’ĕl said to Sha’ul, “I do not return with you, for you have rejected the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rejects you from being meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl.”
15.27: And as Shemu’ĕl turned around to go away, Sha’ul seized the edge of his robe, and it tore.
15.28: And Shemu’ĕl said to him, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has torn the reign of Yisra’ĕl from you today, and has given it to a neighbor of yours, better than you.
15.29: “Moreover, the Eminence of Yisra’ĕl does not lie nor relent. For He is not a man, that He should relent.”
15.30: Then he said, “I have sinned. But esteem me now, please, before the elders of my people and before Yisra’ĕl, and return with me, and I shall bow myself to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.”
15.31: And Shemu’ĕl turned back after Sha’ul, and Sha’ul bowed himself to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.32: And Shemu’ĕl said, “Bring Aḡaḡ meleḵ of the Amalĕqites here to me.” So Aḡaḡ came to him delightedly, and Aḡaḡ said, “Truly, the bitterness of death has turned aside.”
15.33: And Shemu’ĕl said, “As your sword bereaved women, let your mother be bereaved among women too.” Shemu’ĕl then hewed Aḡaḡ to pieces before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in Gilgal.
15.34: And Shemu’ĕl went to Ramah, while Sha’ul went up to his house at Giḇ’ah of Sha’ul.
15.35: And Shemu’ĕl did not see Sha’ul again until the day of his death, for Shemu’ĕl mourned for Sha’ul. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was grieved that He had made Sha’ul to reign over Yisra’ĕl.

16.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Shemu’ĕl, “How long are you going to mourn for Sha’ul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Yisra’ĕl? Fill your horn with oil, and go, I am sending you to Yishai the Bĕyth Leḥemite. For I have seen among his sons a meleḵ for Myself.”
16.2: And Shemu’ĕl said, “How would I go? When Sha’ul hears it, he shall kill me.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, “Take a heifer with you, and say, ‘I have come to slaughter to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’
16.3: “And you shall invite Yishai to the slaughtering, then let Me show you what to do. And you shall anoint for Me the one I say to you.”
16.4: And Shemu’ĕl did what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, and went to Bĕyth Leḥem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, “Do you come in peace?”
16.5: And he said, “In peace. I have come to slaughter to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Qadosh yourselves, and you shall come with me to the slaughtering.” And he qadosh Yishai and his sons, and invited them to the slaughtering.
16.6: And it came to be, when they came, that he saw Eliyaḇ and thought, “The anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is indeed before Him.”
16.7: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Shemu’ĕl, “Do not look at his appearance or at the height of his stature, because I have refused him, for not as man sees, for man looks at the eyes, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 looks at the heart.”
16.8: Then Yishai called Aḇinaḏaḇ, and made him pass before Shemu’ĕl. And he said, “Neither has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chosen this one.”
16.9: Next Yishai made Shammah pass by. And he said, “Neither has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chosen this one.”
16.10: And Yishai made seven of his sons pass before Shemu’ĕl. And Shemu’ĕl said to Yishai, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not chosen these.”
16.11: And Shemu’ĕl said to Yishai, “Are these all the young men?” And he said, “There remains yet the youngest, and see, he is tending the sheep.” And Shemu’ĕl said to Yishai, “Send and bring him, for we do not turn round till he comes here.”
16.12: And he sent and brought him in. And he was tanned, with bright eyes, and good-looking. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, “Arise, anoint him, for this is the one!”
16.13: And Shemu’ĕl took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers. And the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came upon Dawiḏ from that day and onwards. And Shemu’ĕl arose and went to Ramah.
16.14: And the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 turned aside from Sha’ul, and an evil spirit from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 troubled him.
16.15: And the servants of Sha’ul said to him, “Look, now, an evil spirit from Elohim is troubling you.
16.16: “Please, let our master command your servants who are before you, to seek out a man who is a skilled player on the lyre. And it shall be that when the evil spirit from Elohim is upon you, that he shall play with his hand, and you be well.”
16.17: And Sha’ul said to his servants, “Please get me a man that plays well, and bring him to me.”
16.18: And one of the servants answered and said, “Look, I have seen a son of Yishai the Bĕyth Leḥemite, who knows how to play, a brave one, and a man of battle, and skilled in words, and a handsome man. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with him.”
16.19: So Sha’ul sent messengers to Yishai, and said, “Send me your son Dawiḏ, who is with the sheep.”
16.20: And Yishai took a donkey loaded with bread, and a skin of wine, and a young goat, and sent them by his son Dawiḏ to Sha’ul.
16.21: And Dawiḏ came to Sha’ul and stood before him. And he loved him greatly, and he became his armor-bearer.
16.22: Sha’ul therefore sent to Yishai, saying, “Please let Dawiḏ stand before me, for he has found favor in my eyes.”
16.23: And it came to be, whenever the spirit from Elohim was upon Sha’ul, that Dawiḏ would take a lyre and play it with his hand. Then Sha’ul would become refreshed and well, and the evil spirit would leave him.

17.1: And the Pelishtites had gathered their armies for battle, and came together at Soḵoh, which belongs to Yahuḏah, and encamped between Soḵoh and Azĕqah, in Ephes Dammim.
17.2: And Sha’ul and the men of Yisra’ĕl were gathered and encamped in the Valley of Ĕlah, and drew up in battle array to meet the Pelishtites.
17.3: And the Pelishtites stood on a mountain on one side, and Yisra’ĕl stood on a mountain on the other side, with the valley between them.
17.4: Then a champion came out from the camp of the Pelishtites, named Golyath, from Gath, whose height was six ammah and a zereth.
17.5: And a bronze helmet was on his head, and he was armed with a scaled armor, and the weight of the coat was five thousand sheqels of bronze,
17.6: and bronze shin guards on his legs and a bronze spear between his shoulders.
17.7: And the wood of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and his iron spearhead six hundred sheqels, and a shield-bearer went before him.
17.8: And he stood and shouted to the armies of Yisra’ĕl, and said to them, “Why have you come out to line up for battle? Am I not a Pelishtite, and you the servants of Sha’ul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
17.9: “If he is able to fight with me, and shall smite me, then we shall be your servants. But if I overcome him and shall smite him, then you shall be our servants and serve us.”
17.10: Then the Pelishtite said, “This day I shall reproach the armies of Yisra’ĕl. Give me a man, and let us fight together.”
17.11: And Sha’ul and all Yisra’ĕl heard these words of the Pelishtite, and they were broken down and in great fear.
17.12: Now Dawiḏ was the son of that Ephrathite of Bĕyth Leḥem in Yahuḏah, whose name was Yishai, and he had eight sons, and in the days of Sha’ul the man was old among men.
17.13: And the three oldest sons of Yishai went, they had gone to follow Sha’ul to the battle, and the names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eliyaḇ the first-born, and his second Aḇinaḏaḇ, and the third Shammah.
17.14: And Dawiḏ was the youngest. And the three oldest followed Sha’ul,
17.15: but Dawiḏ went and returned from Sha’ul to feed his father’s sheep at Bĕyth Leḥem.
17.16: And for forty days the Pelishtite drew near, morning and evening, and took his stand.
17.17: Then Yishai said to his son Dawiḏ, “Please take to your brothers an ĕphah of this dried grain and these ten loaves, and run to your brothers at the camp.
17.18: “And take these ten cheeses to the commander of the thousand, and see how your brothers are, and bring back news of them.”
17.19: For Sha’ul and they and all the men of Yisra’ĕl were in the Valley of Ĕlah, fighting with the Pelishtites.
17.20: And Dawiḏ rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a herdsman, and took and went as Yishai had commanded him. And he came to the camp as the army was going out to the fight, and they shouted for the battle.
17.21: And Yisra’ĕl and the Pelishtites drew up in battle array, army against army.
17.22: And Dawiḏ left his supplies in the hand of the keeper of the supplies, and ran to the army, and came and greeted his brothers.
17.23: And he was speaking with them and saw the champion, the Pelishtite of Gath, Golyath by name, coming up from the armies of the Pelishtites. And he spoke according to the same words, and Dawiḏ heard.
17.24: And all the men of Yisra’ĕl, when they saw the man, ran from him and were in great fear.
17.25: And the men of Yisra’ĕl said, “Have you seen this man who has come up? For he has come up to reproach Yisra’ĕl. And it shall be that the man who smites him, the meleḵ is going to enrich him with great riches, and give him his daughter, and give his father’s house exemption in Yisra’ĕl.”
17.26: And Dawiḏ spoke to the men who stood by him, saying, “What shall be done for the man who smites this Pelishtite and shall take away reproach from Yisra’ĕl? For who is this uncircumcised Pelishtite, that he should reproach the armies of the living Elohim?”
17.27: And the people answered him according to this word, saying, “This is what is done for the man who smites him.”
17.28: And Eliyaḇ his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men. And Eliyaḇ’s displeasure burned against Dawiḏ, and he said, “Why did you come down here? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your pride and the evil of your heart, for you have come down to see the battle.”
17.29: And Dawiḏ said, “Now what have I done? Was it not but a word?”
17.30: And he turned around from him toward another and said the same word. And these people answered him a word like the first word.
17.31: And when the words which Dawiḏ spoke were heard, they reported them to Sha’ul, and he sent for him.
17.32: And Dawiḏ said to Sha’ul, “Let no man’s heart fail because of him, your servant is going, and shall fight with this Pelishtite.”
17.33: And Sha’ul said to Dawiḏ, “You are not able to go against this Pelishtite to fight with him, for you are but a youth, and he a man of battle from his youth.”
17.34: Then Dawiḏ said to Sha’ul, “Your servant has been tending sheep for his father, and when a lion or a bear came and took a lamb out of the flock,
17.35: I went out after it and smote it, and rescued from its mouth. And when it rose against me, I took hold of its beard, and smote it and killed it.
17.36: “Your servant has smitten both lion and bear. And this uncircumcised Pelishtite shall be like one of them, seeing he has reproached the armies of the living Elohim.”
17.37: And Dawiḏ said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who delivered me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, He delivers me from the hand of this Pelishtite.” And Sha’ul said to Dawiḏ, “Go, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 be with you!”
17.38: And Sha’ul dressed Dawiḏ with his garments, and he put a bronze helmet on his head, and put a coat of armor on him.
17.39: And Dawiḏ girded his sword over his garments, and began to go, but he had not tried them. Then Dawiḏ said to Sha’ul, “I am not able to go with these, for I have not tried them.” So Dawiḏ took them off.
17.40: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose for himself five smooth stones from the wadi, and put them in a shepherd’s bag, in a pouch which he had, and his sling was in his hand. And he drew near to the Pelishtite.
17.41: And the Pelishtite came, and began drawing near to Dawiḏ, and the man who bore the shield went before him.
17.42: And when the Pelishtite looked about and saw Dawiḏ, he despised him, for he was a youth, and tanned and good-looking.
17.43: And the Pelishtite said to Dawiḏ, “Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?” And the Pelishtite cursed Dawiḏ by his mighty ones.
17.44: And the Pelishtite said to Dawiḏ, “Come to me, and I give your flesh to the birds of the shamayim and the beasts of the field!”
17.45: But Dawiḏ said to the Pelishtite, “You come to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a lance. But I come to you in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of the armies of Yisra’ĕl, whom you have reproached.
17.46: “This day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall deliver you into my hand, and I shall smite you and take your head from you, and give the carcasses of the camp of the Pelishtites today to the birds of the shamayim and the wild beasts of the earth, so that all the earth know that Elohim is for Yisra’ĕl,
17.47: and all this assembly know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 does not save with sword and spear, for the battle belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and He shall give you into our hands.”
17.48: And it came to be, when the Pelishtite arose and came and drew near to meet Dawiḏ, that Dawiḏ hurried and ran toward the army to meet the Pelishtite.
17.49: And Dawiḏ put his hand in his bag and took out a stone, and slung it and smote the Pelishtite on his forehead, so that the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.
17.50: Thus Dawiḏ prevailed over the Pelishtite with a sling and a stone, and smote the Pelishtite and killed him, and there was no sword in the hand of Dawiḏ.
17.51: Then Dawiḏ ran and stood over the Pelishtite, and took his sword and drew it out of its sheath and killed him, and cut off his head with it. And when the Pelishtites saw that their champion was dead, they fled.
17.52: And the men of Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah arose and shouted, and pursued the Pelishtites as far as the entrance of the valley and to the gates of Eqron. And the wounded of the Pelishtites fell along the way to Sha’arayim, even as far as Gath and Eqron.
17.53: Then the children of Yisra’ĕl turned back from chasing the Pelishtites, and they plundered their camps.
17.54: And Dawiḏ took the head of the Pelishtite and brought it to Yerushalayim, but he put his weapons in his tent.
17.55: And when Sha’ul saw Dawiḏ going out against the Pelishtite, he said to Aḇnĕr, the commander of the army, “Aḇnĕr, whose son is this youth?” And Aḇnĕr said, “As your being lives, O meleḵ, I do not know.”
17.56: And the meleḵ said, “Ask whose son this young man is.”
17.57: And when Dawiḏ returned from the slaughter of the Pelishtite, Aḇnĕr took him and brought him before Sha’ul with the head of the Pelishtite in his hand.
17.58: And Sha’ul said to him, “Whose son are you, young man?” And Dawiḏ said, “The son of your servant Yishai the Bĕyth Leḥemite.”

18.1: And it came to be, when he had ended speaking to Sha’ul, that the being of Yahonathan was knit to the being of Dawiḏ, and Yahonathan loved him as his own being.
18.2: And Sha’ul took him that day, and would not let him return to his father’s house any more.
18.3: And Yahonathan and Dawiḏ made a covenant, because he loved him as his own being.
18.4: And Yahonathan took off the robe that was on him and gave it to Dawiḏ, and his garments, even to his sword and his bow and his girdle.
18.5: And Dawiḏ went out wherever Sha’ul sent him. He acted wisely, and Sha’ul appointed him over the men of battle, and it was right in the eyes of all the people and also in the eyes of Sha’ul’s servants.
18.6: And it came to be, as they came in, as Dawiḏ was returning from smiting the Pelishtite, that the women came out from all the cities of Yisra’ĕl, singing and dancing, to meet Sha’ul the meleḵ with tambourines, with joy, and with musical instruments.
18.7: And the women sang as they danced, and said, “Sha’ul smote his thousands, and Dawiḏ his ten thousands.”
18.8: And Sha’ul was very wroth, and this matter was evil in his eyes, and he said, “To Dawiḏ they have given ten thousands, and to me they have given thousands. So what more for him, except the reign?”
18.9: And from that day on Sha’ul eyed Dawiḏ.
18.10: And it came to be on the next day that an evil spirit from Elohim came upon Sha’ul, and he naḇu inside the house, while Dawiḏ was playing by his hand, as usual. And the spear was in the hand of Sha’ul.
18.11: Then Sha’ul hurled the spear, for he said, “Let me smite Dawiḏ, even to the wall.” But twice Dawiḏ withdrew from his presence.
18.12: And Sha’ul was afraid of Dawiḏ, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was with him, but from Sha’ul He had turned away.
18.13: Sha’ul therefore removed him from his presence, and made him his commander over a thousand. And he went out and came in before the people.
18.14: And Dawiḏ was acting wisely in all his ways, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was with him.
18.15: And Sha’ul saw that he was acting very wisely, and was afraid of him.
18.16: But all Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah loved Dawiḏ, as he went out and came in before them.
18.17: And Sha’ul said to Dawiḏ, “See my older daughter Mĕraḇ! I give her to you as a wife. Only be brave for me, and fight the battles of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” For Sha’ul thought, “Let not my hand be against him, but let the hand of the Pelishtites be against him.”
18.18: And Dawiḏ said to Sha’ul, “Who am I, and what is my life or my father’s clan in Yisra’ĕl, that I should be son-in-law to the meleḵ?”
18.19: And it came to be at the time when Mĕraḇ, Sha’ul’s daughter, should have been given to Dawiḏ, that she was given to Aḏri’ĕl the Meḥolathite as a wife.
18.20: And Miḵal, Sha’ul’s daughter, loved Dawiḏ. And they told Sha’ul, and the matter was right in his eyes.
18.21: And Sha’ul said, “Let me give her to him and let her be a snare to him, and the hand of the Pelishtites be against him.” So Sha’ul said to Dawiḏ a second time, “Become my son-in-law today.”
18.22: And Sha’ul commanded his servants, “Speak to Dawiḏ gently, and say, ‘See, the meleḵ has delighted in you, and all his servants have loved you. And now, be the meleḵ’s son-in-law!’ ”
18.23: And the servants of Sha’ul spoke those words in the hearing of Dawiḏ. And Dawiḏ said, “Does it seem to you a small matter to be a meleḵ’s son-in-law, seeing I am a poor man, and lightly esteemed?”
18.24: And the servants of Sha’ul told him, saying, “Dawiḏ has spoken according to these words.”
18.25: And Sha’ul said, “Say to Dawiḏ, ‘The meleḵ has no delight in any payment for the bride but one hundred foreskins of the Pelishtites, to take vengeance on the meleḵ’s enemies.’ ” But Sha’ul intended to have Dawiḏ fall by the hand of the Pelishtites.
18.26: And his servants declared these words to Dawiḏ, and it pleased Dawiḏ well to become the meleḵ’s son-in-law. And the days had not expired,
18.27: and Dawiḏ arose and went, he and his men, and smote two hundred men of the Pelishtites. And Dawiḏ brought their foreskins, and they put them before the meleḵ, to become the meleḵ’s son-in-law. And Sha’ul gave him Miḵal his daughter as a wife.
18.28: And Sha’ul saw and knew that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was with Dawiḏ, and Miḵal daughter of Sha’ul loved him.
18.29: So then Sha’ul was still more afraid of Dawiḏ. And Sha’ul came to be an enemy of Dawiḏ all the days.
18.30: And the princes of the Pelishtites went out. And it came to be, whenever they went out, that Dawiḏ acted more wisely than all the servants of Sha’ul, so that his name came to be very precious.

19.1: And Sha’ul spoke to Yahonathan his son and to all his servants, to put Dawiḏ to death. But Yahonathan, Sha’ul’s son, delighted much in Dawiḏ,
19.2: and Yahonathan declared to Dawiḏ, saying, “My father Sha’ul seeks to put you to death. And now, please be on your guard until morning, and dwell in secrecy, and hide.
19.3: “And I myself shall go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and speak with my father about you, and shall see, and shall let you know.”
19.4: And Yahonathan spoke well of Dawiḏ to Sha’ul his father, and said to him, “Let not the meleḵ sin against his servant, against Dawiḏ, because he has not sinned against you, and because his works have been very good toward you.
19.5: “For he took his life in his hands and smote the Pelishtite, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 wrought a great deliverance for all Yisra’ĕl. You saw it and rejoiced. Why then do you sin against innocent blood, to put Dawiḏ to death without cause?”
19.6: And Sha’ul listened to the voice of Yahonathan, and Sha’ul swore, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, he does not die.”
19.7: Yahonathan then called Dawiḏ, and Yahonathan told him all these words. So Yahonathan brought Dawiḏ to Sha’ul, and he was in his presence as before.
19.8: And there was fighting again, and Dawiḏ went out and fought with the Pelishtites, and smote them, a great smiting, and they fled before him.
19.9: And an evil spirit from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came upon Sha’ul as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand. And Dawiḏ was playing by hand,
19.10: and Sha’ul sought to smite the spear through Dawiḏ, and into the wall, but he slipped away from the presence of Sha’ul, so he smote the spear into the wall. And Dawiḏ fled and escaped that night.
19.11: And Sha’ul sent messengers to Dawiḏ’s house to watch him and to put him to death in the morning. And Miḵal, Dawiḏ’s wife, informed him, saying, “If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you are put to death.”
19.12: So Miḵal let Dawiḏ down through a window, and he went and fled and escaped.
19.13: And Miḵal took the household idol and laid it in the bed, and put a cover of goats’ hair for his head, and covered it with a garment.
19.14: And when Sha’ul sent messengers to take Dawiḏ, she said, “He is sick.”
19.15: And Sha’ul sent the messengers back to see Dawiḏ, saying, “Bring him up to me in the bed to put him to death.”
19.16: And the messengers came in and saw the household idol in the bed, with a cover of goats’ hair for his head.
19.17: Sha’ul then said to Miḵal, “Why have you deceived me like this, and sent my enemy away, so that he escaped?” And Miḵal answered Sha’ul, “He said to me, ‘Let me go, why should I put you to death?’ ”
19.18: Now Dawiḏ fled and escaped, and went to Shemu’ĕl at Ramah, and told him all that Sha’ul had done to him. And he and Shemu’ĕl went and dwelt in Nawith.
19.19: And it was reported to Sha’ul, saying, “See, Dawiḏ is in Nawith in Ramah!”
19.20: And Sha’ul sent messengers to take Dawiḏ. And they saw the assembly of the neḇi’im naḇa, and Shemu’ĕl standing as leader over them, and the Ruaḥ of Elohim came upon the messengers of Sha’ul, and they also naḇu.
19.21: And when Sha’ul was told, he sent other messengers, and they naḇu likewise. So Sha’ul sent messengers again, the third time, and they naḇu also.
19.22: Then he himself went to Ramah, and came to the great well that is at Seḵu. And he asked, and said, “Where are Shemu’ĕl and Dawiḏ?” And one said, “There in Nawith in Ramah.”
19.23: So he went there to Nawith in Ramah. And the Ruaḥ of Elohim was upon him too, and he went on and naḇu until he came to Nawith in Ramah.
19.24: And he also stripped off his garments and naḇu before Shemu’ĕl, and lay down naked all that day and all that night. Therefore they say, “Is Sha’ul also among the neḇi’im?”

2.1: And Ḥannah prayed and said, “My heart rejoices in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, my horn has been high in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. My mouth is opened wide over my enemies, for I have rejoiced in Your deliverance.
2.2: “There is no one qodesh like 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for there is no one besides You, and there is no rock like our Elohim.
2.3: “Do not multiply words so proudly, proudly; let no arrogance come from your mouth, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is an Ĕl of knowledge, and by Him deeds are weighed.
2.4: “Bows of the mighty are broken, and those who stumble shall be girded with strength.
2.5: “The satisfied have hired themselves out for bread, and the hungry have ceased. Even the barren has borne seven, and she who has many children pines away.
2.6: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 puts to death and makes alive, He brings down to the grave and raises up.
2.7: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 makes poor and makes rich, He brings low and lifts up.
2.8: “He raises the poor from the dust, He lifts the needy from the dunghill, to sit with princes, and make them inherit a throne of esteem. For the supports of the earth belong to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and He has put the world upon them.
2.9: “He guards the feet of His kind ones, but the wicked are silent in darkness, for man does not become mighty by power.
2.10: “Those who oppose 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are shattered, from the shamayim He thunders against them. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 judges the ends of the earth, and gives strength to His meleḵ, and exalts the horn of His anointed.”
2.11: And Elqanah went to his house at Ramah. But the youth served 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 before Ĕli the kohĕn.
2.12: And the sons of Ĕli were sons of Beliya’al - they did not know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.13: And the ruling of the kohenim with the people was that when any man offered a slaughtering, the kohĕn’s servant shall come with a three-pronged flesh-hook in his hand while the meat was cooking,
2.14: and shall thrust it into the basin, or kettle, or cauldron, or pot. And the kohĕn would take for himself all that the flesh-hook brought up. Thus they did in Shiloh to all the Yisra’ĕlites who came there.
2.15: Also, before they burned the fat, the kohĕn’s servant would come and say to the man who slaughtered, “Give meat for roasting to the kohĕn, for he does not accept cooked meat from you, but raw.”
2.16: And if the man said to him, “Let the fat be burned up first, then take as much as your being desires,” he would then answer him, “No, but give it to me now. And if not, I shall take it by strength.”
2.17: And the sin of the young men was very great before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for the men despised the offering of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.18: But Shemu’ĕl was attending before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 - a youth, wearing a linen shoulder garment.
2.19: And his mother would make him a little robe, and bring it to him year by year when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly slaughtering.
2.20: And Ĕli baraḵ Elqanah and his wife, and said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 give you offspring from this woman for the one she prayed for and gave to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” Then they would go to their own home.
2.21: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 visited Ḥannah, so that she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters, while the young Shemu’ĕl grew before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.22: And Ĕli was very old, and had heard all that his sons were doing to all Yisra’ĕl, and how they lay with the women who were assembling at the door of the Tent of Appointment.
2.23: And he said to them, “Why do you do deeds like these? For I hear of your evil deeds from all the people.
2.24: “No, my sons! For it is not a good report that I hear: making the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 transgress.
2.25: “If one man sins against another, Elohim shall judge him. But if a man sins against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who shall pray for him?” But they did not listen to the voice of their father, though it pleased 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to put them to death.
2.26: And the young Shemu’ĕl was growing in stature, and was in favor with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and also with men.
2.27: And a man of Elohim came to Ĕli and said to him, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Did I not clearly reveal Myself to the house of your father when they were in Mitsrayim in Pharaoh’s house,
2.28: even to choose him out of all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl to be My kohĕn, to offer upon My altar, to burn incense, and to wear a shoulder garment before Me? And did I not give to the house of your father all the offerings of the children of Yisra’ĕl made by fire?
2.29: ‘Why do you kick at My slaughtering and My offering which I have commanded in My Mishkan, and esteem your sons above Me, to make yourselves fat with the best of all the offerings of Yisra’ĕl My people?’
2.30: “Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl declares, ‘I said indeed that your house and the house of your father would walk before Me forever.’ But now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 declares, ‘Far be it from Me, for those who esteem Me I esteem, and those who despise Me are accursed.
2.31: ‘See, the days are coming that I shall cut off your arm and the arm of your father’s house, so that an old man shall not be in your house.
2.32: ‘And you shall see an enemy in My Mishkan, despite all the good which He does for Yisra’ĕl, and there shall not be an old man in your house forever.
2.33: ‘But any of your men whom I do not cut off from My altar is to consume your eyes and grieve your life, and all the increase of your house die as men.
2.34: ‘And this is the sign to you that comes upon your two sons, upon Ḥophni and Pineḥas: in one day they are going to die, both of them.
2.35: ‘And I shall raise up for Myself a trustworthy kohĕn who does according to what is in My heart and in My being. And I shall build him a steadfast house, and he shall walk before My anointed forever.
2.36: ‘And it shall be that everyone who is left in your house shall come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a cake of bread, and say, “Please, put me in one of the kehunnah positions to eat a piece of bread.” ’ ”

20.1: And Dawiḏ fled from Nawith in Ramah, and went and said to Yahonathan, “What have I done? What is my wickedness, and what is my sin before your father, that he seeks my life?”
20.2: And Yahonathan said to him, “Far be it! You are not going to die! See, my father does no big matter nor small matter without disclosing it to me. And why should my father hide this matter from me? It is not so!”
20.3: But Dawiḏ swore again, and said, “Your father knows well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he says, ‘Do not let Yahonathan know this, lest he be grieved.’ But truly, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives and as your being lives, there is but a step between me and death.”
20.4: And Yahonathan said to Dawiḏ, “Whatever your desire is, I do it for you.”
20.5: And Dawiḏ said to Yahonathan, “See, tomorrow is the New Moon, and I ought to sit with the meleḵ to eat. But let me go, and I shall hide in the field until the third day at evening.
20.6: “If your father misses me at all, then you shall say, ‘Dawiḏ earnestly asked my permission to run over to Bĕyth Leḥem, his city, for a yearly slaughtering is made there for all the clan.’
20.7: “If he says thus, ‘It is well,’ your servant is safe. But if he is very displeased, then know that he has resolved to do evil.
20.8: “And you shall show kindness to your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with you. And if there is wickedness in me, put me to death yourself, for why should you bring me to your father?”
20.9: And Yahonathan said, “Far be it from you! For if I knew with certainty that my father has resolved that evil is to come upon you, then would I not make it known to you?”
20.10: And Dawiḏ said to Yahonathan, “Who would make it known to me, or what if your father answers you sharply?”
20.11: And Yahonathan said to Dawiḏ, “Come, and let us go out into the field.” And they both went out into the field.
20.12: And Yahonathan said to Dawiḏ, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl! When I search out my father sometime tomorrow, or the third day, and see if there is good toward Dawiḏ, and I do not send to you or disclose it to you,
20.13: so let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 do so and much more to Yahonathan. And if it pleases my father to do you evil, then I shall disclose it to you and send you away, and you shall go in peace. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 be with you as He has been with my father.
20.14: “But show me the kindness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, not only while I still live, so that I do not die,
20.15: and do not cut off your kindness from my house forever, no, not when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has cut off every one of the enemies of Dawiḏ from the face of the earth.”
20.16: And Yahonathan made a covenant with the house of Dawiḏ: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall require it at the hand of the enemies of Dawiḏ.”
20.17: And Yahonathan again made Dawiḏ swear, because he loved him, for he loved him as he loved his own being.
20.18: So Yahonathan said to him, “Tomorrow is the New Moon, and you shall be missed, because your seat shall be empty.
20.19: “And on the third day, go down quickly and you shall come to the place where you hid on the day of the deed, and shall remain by the stone of Ezel.
20.20: “And let me shoot three arrows to the side of it as though shooting at a target,
20.21: and see, I shall send the youth, saying, ‘Go, find the arrows.’ If I expressly say to the youth, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you, get them and come,’ then, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, there is safety for you and no concern.
20.22: “But if I say thus to the youth, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ go your way, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sent you away.
20.23: “And as for the word which you and I have spoken of, see, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is between you and me forever.”
20.24: And Dawiḏ hid in the field. And when the New Moon came, the meleḵ sat down by the food to eat.
20.25: And the meleḵ sat on his seat, as at other times, on a seat by the wall, with Yahonathan standing, and Aḇnĕr sitting by Sha’ul’s side, but the place of Dawiḏ was empty.
20.26: But Sha’ul did not speak anything that day, for he thought, “It is an accident; he is not clean, for he has not been cleansed.”
20.27: And it came to be the next day, the second of the month, that Dawiḏ’s place was empty. And Sha’ul said to Yahonathan his son, “Why has the son of Yishai not come to eat, either yesterday or today?”
20.28: And Yahonathan answered Sha’ul, “Dawiḏ earnestly asked for leave to Bĕyth Leḥem.
20.29: “And he said, ‘Please let me go, for our clan has a slaughtering in the city, and my brother has commanded me to be there. And now, if I have found favor in your eyes, please let me get away and see my brothers.’ That is why he has not come to the meleḵ’s table.”
20.30: Then the displeasure of Sha’ul burned against Yahonathan, and he said to him, “You son of a perverse, rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Yishai to your own shame and to the shame of your mother’s nakedness?
20.31: “For as long as the son of Yishai lives on the earth, you shall not be established, you and your malḵuth. And now, send and bring him to me, for he is a son of death.”
20.32: And Yahonathan answered Sha’ul his father, and said to him, “Why should he be put to death? What has he done?”
20.33: At that, Sha’ul hurled a spear at him to smite him. Then Yahonathan knew that his father had resolved to put Dawiḏ to death.
20.34: And Yahonathan rose up from the table in the heat of displeasure, and ate no food the second day of the month, for he was grieved for Dawiḏ, because his father put him to shame.
20.35: And it came to be, in the morning, that Yahonathan went out into the field at the time appointed with Dawiḏ, and a small youth was with him.
20.36: And he said to the youth, “Now run, find the arrows which I shoot.” As the youth ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.
20.37: And when the youth came to the place where the arrow was which Yahonathan had shot, Yahonathan called out after the youth and said, “Is not the arrow beyond you?”
20.38: And Yahonathan shouted after the youth, “Make haste, hurry, do not stand still!” And Yahonathan’s youth picked up the arrows and came to his master.
20.39: But the youth knew not a speck. Only Yahonathan and Dawiḏ knew of the matter.
20.40: Then Yahonathan gave his weapons to the youth and said to him, “Go, take them to the city.”
20.41: And as soon as the youth had gone, Dawiḏ rose up from the south side, and fell on his face to the ground, and bowed down three times. And they kissed one another. And they wept together, but Dawiḏ more so.
20.42: And Yahonathan said to Dawiḏ, “Go in peace, since we have both sworn in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saying, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is between you and me, and between your seed and my seed, forever.’ ” Then he arose and left, and Yahonathan went into the city.

21.1: And Dawiḏ came to Noḇ, to Aḥimeleḵ the kohĕn. And Aḥimeleḵ trembled when he met Dawiḏ, and asked him, “Why are you alone, and no one is with you?”
21.2: And Dawiḏ said to Aḥimeleḵ the kohĕn, “The meleḵ has commanded me a word, and said to me, ‘Let no one know whatever of the word about which I send you, and which I have commanded you.’ And I have directed my young men to such and such a place.
21.3: “And now, what do you have on hand? Give five loaves into my hand, or whatever is found.”
21.4: And the kohĕn answered Dawiḏ and said, “There is no ordinary bread on hand, but there is qodesh bread - provided the young men have kept themselves from women.”
21.5: And Dawiḏ answered the kohĕn, and said to him, “Truly, women have been kept from us about three days since I came out. And the vessels of the young men are qodesh, and it is an ordinary mission, and also, it was qodesh in the vessel today.”
21.6: Then the kohĕn gave him qodesh bread, for there was no bread there except the showbread which had been taken from before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in order to put hot bread in on the day it is taken away.
21.7: Now one of the servants of Sha’ul was there that day, detained before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And his name was Do’ĕḡ, an Eḏomite, the chief of the herdsmen who belonged to Sha’ul.
21.8: And Dawiḏ said to Aḥimeleḵ, “Is there not here on hand a spear or a sword? For I have brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the matter of the meleḵ was urgent.”
21.9: And the kohĕn said, “The sword of Golyath the Pelishtite, whom you smote in the Valley of Ĕlah. See, it is wrapped in a garment behind the shoulder garment. If you would take it, take it. For there is none other except this one here.” And Dawiḏ said, “There is none like it, give it to me.”
21.10: And Dawiḏ rose and fled that day from before Sha’ul, and went to Aḵish the meleḵ of Gath.
21.11: But the servants of Aḵish said to him, “Is this not Dawiḏ the meleḵ of the land? Did they not sing of him to each other in dances, saying, ‘Sha’ul smote his thousands, and Dawiḏ his ten thousands’?”
21.12: And Dawiḏ took these words to heart, and was very much afraid of Aḵish the meleḵ of Gath,
21.13: and changed his behavior before them, and feigned madness in their hands, and scratched on the doors of the gate, and let his saliva run down on his beard.
21.14: Then Aḵish said to his servants, “Look, you see the man is acting like a madman. Why do you bring him to me?
21.15: “Am I short of madmen, that you have brought this one to act as a madman near me? Should this one come into my house?”

22.1: And Dawiḏ went from there and escaped to the cave of Aḏullam. And his brothers and all his father’s house heard it, and went down to him there.
22.2: And everyone who was in distress, everyone who was in debt, and everyone bitter in being gathered to him. So he became head over them, and there were about four hundred men with him.
22.3: And Dawiḏ went from there to Mitspĕh of Mo’aḇ and said to the meleḵ of Mo’aḇ, “Please let my father and mother come here with you, till I know what Elohim does for me.”
22.4: And he left them with the meleḵ of Mo’aḇ, and they dwelt with him all the time that Dawiḏ was in the stronghold.
22.5: And the naḇi Gaḏ said to Dawiḏ, “Do not remain in the stronghold. Leave, and go to the land of Yahuḏah.” So Dawiḏ left and went into the Ḥereth woods.
22.6: And Sha’ul heard that Dawiḏ and the men who were with him had been discovered, while Sha’ul was in Giḇ’ah, sitting under a tamarisk tree in Ramah, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants standing about him.
22.7: And Sha’ul said to his servants who were standing around him, “Hear now, you Binyamites! Does the son of Yishai give every one of you fields and vineyards, and make you all commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?
22.8: “For all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who reveals to me that my son has made a covenant with the son of Yishai. And there is not one of you who is grieved for me or reveals to me that my son has stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as it is this day.”
22.9: And Do’ĕḡ the Eḏomite, who was put over the servants of Sha’ul, answered and said, “I saw the son of Yishai going to Noḇ, to Aḥimeleḵ son of Aḥituḇ.
22.10: “And he inquired of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for him, gave him food, and gave him the sword of Golyath the Pelishtite.”
22.11: And the meleḵ sent someone to call Aḥimeleḵ the kohĕn, son of Aḥituḇ, and all his father’s house, the kohenim who were in Noḇ. And they all came to the meleḵ,
22.12: and Sha’ul said, “Hear now, son of Aḥituḇ!” And he answered, “Here I am, my master.”
22.13: And Sha’ul said to him, “Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Yishai, by giving him bread and a sword, and have inquired of Elohim for him, to rise against me, to lie in wait, as it is this day?”
22.14: And Aḥimeleḵ answered the meleḵ and said, “And who among all your servants is so trustworthy as Dawiḏ, who is the meleḵ’s son-in-law, and has turned aside to your counsel, and is esteemed in your house?
22.15: “Have I today begun to inquire of Elohim for him? Far be it from me! Let not the meleḵ lay a case against his servant, or against any in the house of my father. For your servant knew not of all this, little or much.”
22.16: And the meleḵ said, “You shall certainly die, Aḥimeleḵ, you and all your father’s house!”
22.17: The meleḵ then said to the guards who stood about him, “Turn and put the kohenim of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to death, because their hand also is with Dawiḏ, and because they knew when he fled and did not reveal it to me.” But the servants of the meleḵ would not lift their hands to come against the kohenim of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.18: And the meleḵ said to Do’ĕḡ, “You turn and come against the kohenim!” So Do’ĕḡ the Eḏomite turned and came against the kohenim, and put to death on that day eighty-five men who wore a linen shoulder garment.
22.19: And he smote Noḇ, the city of the kohenim, with the edge of the sword, from men even to women, from children even to nursing infants, and oxen and donkeys and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
22.20: And one of the sons of Aḥimeleḵ son of Aḥituḇ, named Eḇyathar, escaped and fled after Dawiḏ.
22.21: And Eḇyathar reported to Dawiḏ that Sha’ul had slain the kohenim of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.22: And Dawiḏ said to Eḇyathar, “I knew that day, when Do’ĕḡ the Eḏomite was there, that he would certainly inform Sha’ul. I am accountable for all the lives of your father’s house.
22.23: “Remain with me, do not fear. For he who seeks my life seeks your life, but with me you are safe.”

23.1: And they informed Dawiḏ, saying, “See, the Pelishtites are fighting against Qe’ilah, and they are plundering the threshing-floors.”
23.2: So Dawiḏ inquired of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, “Shall I go and smite these Pelishtites?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Dawiḏ, “Go and smite the Pelishtites, and save Qe’ilah.”
23.3: And Dawiḏ’s men said to him, “See, we here in Yahuḏah are afraid. How much more, then, if we go to Qe’ilah against the armies of the Pelishtites?”
23.4: And Dawiḏ inquired of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 once again. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 answered him and said, “Arise, go down to Qe’ilah, for I am giving the Pelishtites into your hand.”
23.5: So Dawiḏ and his men went to Qe’ilah and fought with the Pelishtites, and he led away their livestock and smote them, a great smiting. Thus Dawiḏ saved the inhabitants of Qe’ilah.
23.6: And it came to be, when Eḇyathar son of Aḥimeleḵ fled to Dawiḏ at Qe’ilah, that he went down with a shoulder garment in his hand.
23.7: And Sha’ul was informed that Dawiḏ had gone to Qe’ilah. Then Sha’ul said, “Elohim has estranged him into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a town that has gates and bars.”
23.8: And Sha’ul summoned all the people to battle, to go down, to Qe’ilah to besiege Dawiḏ and his men.
23.9: And Dawiḏ knew that Sha’ul was plotting evil against him, and said to Eḇyathar the kohĕn, “Bring the shoulder garment here.”
23.10: And Dawiḏ said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, Your servant has heard for certain that Sha’ul seeks to come to Qe’ilah to destroy the city for my sake.
23.11: “Are the landowners of Qe’ilah going to surrender me into his hand? Is Sha’ul coming down, as Your servant has heard? O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, I pray, let Your servant know.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, “He is coming down.”
23.12: And Dawiḏ said, “Are the land-owners of Qe’ilah going to surrender me and my men into the hand of Sha’ul?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, “They are going to surrender you.”
23.13: Then Dawiḏ and his men, about six hundred, arose and left Qe’ilah and went wherever they could go. And Sha’ul was informed that Dawiḏ had escaped from Qe’ilah, and he ceased to go out.
23.14: And Dawiḏ remained in the wilderness, in strongholds, and remained in the hill country in the Wilderness of Ziph. And Sha’ul sought him every day, but Elohim did not give him into his hand.
23.15: And Dawiḏ saw that Sha’ul had come out to seek his life while Dawiḏ was in the Wilderness of Ziph at Ḥoresh.
23.16: And Yahonathan, Sha’ul’s son, arose and went to Dawiḏ at Ḥoresh and strengthened his hand in Elohim,
23.17: and said to him, “Do not fear, for the hand of Sha’ul my father is not going to find you, and you are to reign over Yisra’ĕl, and I am to be next to you. Even my father Sha’ul knows that.”
23.18: And they made a covenant before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And Dawiḏ remained at Ḥoresh while Yahonathan went to his own house.
23.19: And the Ziphites came up to Sha’ul at Giḇ’ah, saying, “Is Dawiḏ not hiding with us in the strongholds of Ḥoresh, in the hill of Ḥaḵilah, which is on the south of the wasteland?
23.20: “And now, O meleḵ, by all the desire of your being, come down, come down, and our part is to surrender him into the meleḵ’s hand.”
23.21: And Sha’ul said, “Beruḵim are you of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for you have sympathy with me.
23.22: “Please go, prepare yet further and find out and see the place where his hide-out is, who has seen him there. For I am told that he is very cunning.
23.23: “So look, and learn all about the hiding places where he hides. And you shall come back to me with certainty, then I shall go with you. And it shall be, if he is in the land, that I shall search for him throughout all the clans of Yahuḏah.”
23.24: And they rose up and went to Ziph before Sha’ul, while Dawiḏ and his men were in the Wilderness of Ma’on, in the desert plain on the south of the wasteland.
23.25: And Sha’ul and his men went to seek him, and they informed Dawiḏ, so he went down to the rock, and remained in the Wilderness of Ma’on. And when Sha’ul heard this, he pursued Dawiḏ in the Wilderness of Ma’on.
23.26: And Sha’ul went on one side of the mountain, and Dawiḏ and his men on the other side of the mountain. And Dawiḏ was hurrying to get away from Sha’ul, for Sha’ul and his men were surrounding Dawiḏ and his men to take them.
23.27: Then a messenger came to Sha’ul, saying, “Hurry and come, for the Pelishtites have invaded the land!”
23.28: So Sha’ul turned back from pursuing Dawiḏ, and went against the Pelishtites. Therefore they called that place Sela ha’Maḥleqoth.
23.29: And Dawiḏ went up from there and remained in strongholds at Ĕyn Geḏi.

24.1: And it came to be, when Sha’ul had returned from pursuing the Pelishtites, that it was reported to him, saying, “See, Dawiḏ is in the Wilderness of Ĕyn Geḏi.”
24.2: So Sha’ul took three thousand chosen men from all Yisra’ĕl, and went to seek Dawiḏ and his men on the face of Tsurĕy ha’Ye’Ĕylim.
24.3: And he came to the sheepfolds, on the way, and there was a cave. And Sha’ul went in to relieve himself. Now Dawiḏ and his men were sitting in the sides of the cave.
24.4: And the men of Dawiḏ said to him, “See, the day of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to you, ‘See, I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as it seems good to you!’ ” And Dawiḏ arose and gently cut off a corner of Sha’ul’s robe.
24.5: And it came to be afterward that the heart of Dawiḏ smote him because he had cut the robe of Sha’ul.
24.6: So he said to his men, “Far be it from me, by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that I should do this matter to my master, anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to stretch out my hand against him, for he is the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
24.7: And Dawiḏ dispersed his servants with words, and did not allow them to rise against Sha’ul. And Sha’ul rose up from the cave and went on his way.
24.8: And afterward Dawiḏ arose and went out of the cave, and called out to Sha’ul, saying, “My master the meleḵ!” And when Sha’ul looked behind him, Dawiḏ bowed with his face to the earth, and did obeisance.
24.9: And Dawiḏ said to Sha’ul, “Why do you listen to the words of men who say, ‘See, Dawiḏ seeks to do you evil’?
24.10: “See, this day your eyes have seen that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gave you today into my hand in the cave, and one said to slay you. But my eye pardoned you, and I said, ‘I do not stretch out my hand against my master, for he is the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’
24.11: “And my father, see! Even see the corner of your robe in my hand! For in that I cut off the corner of your robe, and did not slay you, know and see that there is neither evil nor rebellion in my hand, and I have not sinned against you, while you are hunting my life to take it.
24.12: “Let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 judge between you and me, and let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 revenge me on you, but my hand is not against you.
24.13: “As the proverb of the ancients says, ‘Wickedness comes from the wicked.’ But my hand is not against you.
24.14: “After whom has the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl come out? Whom do you pursue? A dead dog? A flea?
24.15: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall be judge, and rightly rule between you and me, and see and plead my case, and rightly rule me out of your hand.”
