24.16: And it came to be, when Dawiḏ had ended speaking these words to Sha’ul, that Sha’ul said, “Is this your voice, my son Dawiḏ?” So Sha’ul lifted up his voice and wept.
24.17: And he said to Dawiḏ, “You are more righteous than I, for you have rewarded me with good, whereas I have rewarded you with evil.
24.18: “And you have shown today how you have done good to me, for when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 surrendered me into your hand you did not slay me.
24.19: “For if a man finds his enemy, shall he let him get away safely? And let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 reward you with good for what you have done to me today.
24.20: “And now look, I know that you shall certainly reign, and that the reign of Yisra’ĕl shall be established in your hand.
24.21: “And now, swear to me by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that you do not cut off my seed after me, nor destroy my name from my father’s house.”
24.22: And Dawiḏ swore to Sha’ul. Then Sha’ul went home, and Dawiḏ and his men went up to the stronghold.

25.1: And Shemu’ĕl died, and all Yisra’ĕl gathered and mourned for him, and buried him at his home in Ramah. And Dawiḏ arose and went down into the Wilderness of Paran.
25.2: Now there was a man in Ma’on and his work was in Karmel, and the man was very great. And he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. And he came to be shearing his sheep in Karmel.
25.3: And the name of the man was Naḇal, and the name of his wife Aḇiḡayil. And she was a woman of good understanding and good-looking. But the man was hard and evil in his doings. And he was of Kalĕḇ.
25.4: And Dawiḏ heard in the wilderness that Naḇal was shearing his sheep.
25.5: And Dawiḏ sent ten young men, and Dawiḏ said to the young men, “Go up to Karmel, and you shall come to Naḇal, and greet him in my name,
25.6: and say this, ‘Long life and peace to you! And peace to your house, and peace to all that you have!
25.7: ‘And now, I have heard that you have shearers. Now your shepherds have been with us. We did not put them to shame, and not a speck of theirs was missing all the days they were in Karmel.
25.8: ‘Ask your young men, and let them inform you. So let the young men find favor in your eyes, for we come on a good day. Please give whatever comes to your hand to your servants and to your son Dawiḏ.’ ”
25.9: And the young men of Dawiḏ came and spoke to Naḇal according to all these words in the name of Dawiḏ, and waited.
25.10: But Naḇal answered the servants of Dawiḏ and said, “Who is Dawiḏ, and who is the son of Yishai? The servants who are running away from their masters, have become many nowadays.
25.11: “And shall I take my bread and my water and my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men coming from who knows where?”
25.12: And the young men of Dawiḏ turned around on their way and went back, and came and reported to him all these words.
25.13: And Dawiḏ said to his men, “Each one gird on his sword.” So they each girded on his sword, and Dawiḏ also girded on his sword. And about four hundred men went with Dawiḏ, and two hundred remained with the baggage.
25.14: And one of the young men informed Aḇiḡayil, the wife of Naḇal, saying, “See, Dawiḏ sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but he scoffed at them.
25.15: “But the men were very good to us, and did not put us to shame, nor did we miss anything all the days we accompanied them, when we were in the fields.
25.16: “They were a wall to us both by night and day, all the days we were with them tending the sheep.
25.17: “And now, know and see what you should do, for evil has been resolved against our master, and against all his household, and he is too much of a son of Beliya’al to speak to.”
25.18: Then Aḇiḡayil made haste and took two hundred loaves, and two skins of wine, and five sheep made ready, five se’im of roasted grain, and one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and loaded them on donkeys.
25.19: And she said to her servants, “Pass over before me. See, I am coming after you.” But she did not inform her husband Naḇal.
25.20: And it came to be, as she rode on the donkey, that she went down under cover of the hill, and there were Dawiḏ and his men, coming down toward her, and she met them.
25.21: And Dawiḏ had said, “Only in vain have I protected all that this one has in the wilderness, so that not a speck was missing of all that belongs to him. And he has repaid me evil for good.
25.22: “Let Elohim do so, and more also, to the enemies of Dawiḏ, if I leave one male of all who belong to him by morning light.”
25.23: And Aḇiḡayil saw Dawiḏ, and she hastened to come down from the donkey, and fell on her face before Dawiḏ, and bowed down to the ground,
25.24: and fell at his feet and said, “On me, my master, let this wickedness be on me! And please let your female servant speak in your ears, and hear the words of your female servant.
25.25: “Please, let not my master regard this man of Beliya’al, Naḇal. For as his name is, so is he: Naḇal is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your female servant, did not see the young men of my master whom you sent.
25.26: “And now my master, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives and as your being lives, since 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has withheld you from coming to bloodshed and from avenging yourself with your own hand, now then, let your enemies be as Naḇal, even those seeking evil against my master.
25.27: “And now this present which your female servant has brought to my master, let it be given to the young men who follow my master.
25.28: “Please bear the transgression of your female servant. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is certainly making a steadfast house for my master, because my master fights the battles of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and evil is not found in you in your days.
25.29: “And if a man rises to pursue you and seek your life, and the life of my master has been bound in the bundle of the living with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, then the lives of your enemies He shall sling out, as from the pocket of a sling.
25.30: “And it shall be, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has done for my master according to all the good that He has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you ruler over Yisra’ĕl,
25.31: do not let this be a staggering and stumbling of heart to my master, that you have shed blood without cause, or that my master has saved himself. And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has done good to my master, then remember your female servant.”
25.32: And Dawiḏ said to Aḇiḡayil, “Baruḵ be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, who sent you to meet me today!
25.33: “And baruḵ is your good taste, and beruḵah are you, because you have kept me this day from coming to bloodshed and from avenging myself with my own hand.
25.34: “Nevertheless, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl lives, who has kept me back from doing evil to you, if you had not hurried and come to meet me, not a male would have been left to Naḇal by break of day, for certain.”
25.35: And Dawiḏ received from her hand what she had brought him, and said to her, “Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and have accepted your face.”
25.36: And Aḇiḡayil went to Naḇal, and see, he was at a feast in his house, like the feast of a meleḵ. And Naḇal’s heart was glad within him, and he was exceedingly drunk. So she told him not a word, little or much, until morning light.
25.37: And it came to be, in the morning, when the wine had gone from Naḇal, and his wife had told him these matters, that his heart died within him, and he became like a stone.
25.38: And it came to be in about ten days, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 smote Naḇal, and he died.
25.39: And Dawiḏ heard that Naḇal was dead, and he said, “Baruḵ be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who has pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Naḇal, and has kept His servant from evil! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has returned the evil of Naḇal on his own head.” And Dawiḏ sent and spoke to Aḇiḡayil, to take her as his wife.
25.40: And when the servants of Dawiḏ had come to Aḇiḡayil at Karmel, they spoke to her saying, “Dawiḏ sent us to you, to ask you to become his wife.”
25.41: And she arose, bowed her face to the earth, and said, “Here is your female servant, a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my master.”
25.42: And Aḇiḡayil hurried and rose, and rode on a donkey, with five of her female attendants. And she followed the messengers of Dawiḏ, and became his wife.
25.43: Dawiḏ had also taken Aḥino’am of Yizre’ĕl, and so both of them were his wives.
25.44: But Sha’ul had given Miḵal his daughter, Dawiḏ’s wife, to Palti son of Layish, who was from Gallim.

26.1: And the Ziphites came to Sha’ul at Giḇ’ah, saying, “Is not Dawiḏ hiding himself in the hill of Ḥaḵilah, overlooking the wasteland?”
26.2: And Sha’ul rose up and went down to the Wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men of Yisra’ĕl, to seek Dawiḏ in the Wilderness of Ziph.
26.3: And Sha’ul encamped in the hill of Ḥaḵilah, overlooking the wasteland, by the way, while Dawiḏ was dwelling in the wilderness, and he saw that Sha’ul came after him into the wilderness.
26.4: And Dawiḏ sent out spies, and learned that Sha’ul had indeed come.
26.5: And Dawiḏ rose up and came to the place where Sha’ul had encamped. And Dawiḏ saw the place where Sha’ul lay, and Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, the commander of his army. And Sha’ul was lying within the enclosure, with the people encamped all around him.
26.6: And Dawiḏ spoke up and said to Aḥimeleḵ the Ḥittite and to Aḇishai son of Tseruyah, brother of Yo’aḇ, saying, “Who goes down with me to Sha’ul in the camp?” And Aḇishai said, “I, I go down with you.”
26.7: And Dawiḏ and Aḇishai came to the people by night and saw Sha’ul lying asleep within the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head, and Aḇnĕr and the people lay all around him.
26.8: And Aḇishai said to Dawiḏ, “Elohim has surrendered your enemy into your hand this day. And now, please, let me smite him at once with the spear, right into the earth, and not a second time!”
26.9: But Dawiḏ said to Aḇishai, “Do not destroy him, for who shall stretch out his hand against the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and be guiltless?”
26.10: Dawiḏ also said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, except 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 smites him, or his day come that he shall die, or he shall go out to battle and perish,
26.11: far be it from me, by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that I stretch out my hand against the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And now, please take the spear and the jug of water that are by his head, and let us go.”
26.12: So Dawiḏ took the spear and the jug of water by Sha’ul’s head, and they went away. And no man saw it or knew it or awoke, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had fallen on them.
26.13: And Dawiḏ passed over to the other side, and stood on the top of a hill far away, a great distance being between them.
26.14: And Dawiḏ called out to the people and to Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, saying, “Do you not answer, Aḇnĕr?” And Aḇnĕr answered and said, “Who are you, calling out to the meleḵ?”
26.15: And Dawiḏ said to Aḇnĕr, “Are you not a man? And who is like you in Yisra’ĕl? Why then have you not guarded your master the meleḵ? For one of the people came in to destroy your master the meleḵ.
26.16: “What you have done is not good. As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, you are worthy to die, because you have not guarded your master, the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And now see where the meleḵ’s spear is, and the jug of water that was by his head.”
26.17: And Sha’ul recognized Dawiḏ’s voice, and said, “Is that your voice, my son Dawiḏ?” And Dawiḏ said, “It is my voice, my master, O meleḵ.”
26.18: And he said, “Why is this that my master is pursuing his servant? For what have I done, or what evil is in my hand?
26.19: “And now, please, let my master the meleḵ hear the words of his servant: If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has moved you against me, let Him accept an offering. But if it is the children of men, then they are cursed before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for they have driven me out today that I should not join myself to the inheritance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, ‘Go, serve other mighty ones.’
26.20: “And now, do not let my blood fall to the earth before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. For the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl has come out to seek a flea, as when one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”
26.21: And Sha’ul said, “I have sinned. Come back, my son Dawiḏ. For no more am I going to do evil to you, because my life was precious in your eyes today. See, I have acted foolishly, and have greatly strayed.”
26.22: And Dawiḏ answered and said, “See, the meleḵ’s spear! And let one of the young men come over and get it.
26.23: “And let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 reward every man for his righteousness and his trustworthiness, for this day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gave you into my hand, but I would not stretch out my hand against the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
26.24: “And see, as your life has been valued in my eyes today, so let my life be valued in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and let Him deliver me out of all distress.”
26.25: And Sha’ul said to Dawiḏ, “Baruḵ are you, my son Dawiḏ, achieving much, and indeed prevailing!” Then Dawiḏ went on his way, and Sha’ul returned to his place.

27.1: And Dawiḏ said in his heart, “Now I shall perish by the hand of Sha’ul, some day. There is naught better for me than to escape to the land of the Pelishtites. Then Sha’ul shall give up searching for me any longer in any part of Yisra’ĕl, and I shall escape out of his hand.”
27.2: So Dawiḏ rose up and passed over with the six hundred men who were with him to Aḵish son of Ma’oḵ, meleḵ of Gath.
27.3: And Dawiḏ dwelt with Aḵish at Gath, he and his men, each man with his household - Dawiḏ with his two wives, Aḥino’am the Yizre’ĕlitess, and Aḇiḡayil the Karmelitess, Naḇal’s widow.
27.4: And it was reported to Sha’ul that Dawiḏ had fled to Gath, so he sought him no more.
27.5: And Dawiḏ said to Aḵish, “If I have now found favor in your eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, to dwell there. For why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?”
27.6: And Aḵish gave him Tsiqlaḡ that day. That is why Tsiqlaḡ has belonged to the melaḵim of Yahuḏah to this day.
27.7: And the time that Dawiḏ dwelt in the country of the Pelishtites came to be a year and four months.
27.8: And Dawiḏ and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, and the Girzites, and the Amalĕqites. For those nations were the inhabitants of the land from of old, as you go to Shur, even as far as the land of Mitsrayim.
27.9: And when Dawiḏ had smitten the land, he left neither man nor woman alive, but took away sheep, and cattle, and donkeys, and camels, and garments, and returned and came to Aḵish.
27.10: And Aḵish would say, “Where have you made a raid today?” And Dawiḏ would say, “Against the South of Yahuḏah, or against the South of the Yeraḥme’ĕlites, or against the South of the Qĕynites.”
27.11: Dawiḏ did not keep alive man nor woman, to bring news to Gath, saying, “Lest they inform against us, saying, ‘Thus Dawiḏ did.’ ” And this was his practice all the days that he dwelt in the country of the Pelishtites.
27.12: And Aḵish trusted Dawiḏ, saying, “He has indeed made himself a stench to his people in Yisra’ĕl, and has become my servant forever.”

28.1: And it came to be in those days that the Pelishtites gathered their armies for battle, to fight with Yisra’ĕl. And Aḵish said to Dawiḏ, “You know, of course, that you are to go out with me in the army, you and your men.”
28.2: And Dawiḏ said to Aḵish, “Very well, you shall know what your servant should do.” And Aḵish said to Dawiḏ, “Very well, I make you one of my chief guardians forever.”
28.3: And Shemu’ĕl had died, and all Yisra’ĕl had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, in his own city. And Sha’ul had put away the mediums and the spiritists from the land.
28.4: And the Pelishtites were gathered, and came and encamped at Shunĕm. And Sha’ul gathered all Yisra’ĕl, and they encamped at Gilboa.
28.5: And when Sha’ul saw the army of the Pelishtites, he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.
28.6: And Sha’ul inquired of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 did not answer him, either by dreams or by Urim or by the neḇi’im.
28.7: Sha’ul then said to his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, to go to her and inquire of her.” And his servants said to him, “Look, there is a woman who is a medium at Ĕyn Dor.”
28.8: And Sha’ul disguised himself and put on other garments, and went, he and two men with him. And they came to the woman by night. And he said, “Please divine for me, and bring up for me the one I shall name.”
28.9: But the woman said to him, “Look, you know what Sha’ul has done, how he has cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Why then do you lay a snare for my life, to put me to death?”
28.10: And Sha’ul swore to her by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, no punishment comes upon you for this matter.”
28.11: And the woman said, “Whom do I bring up for you?” So he said, “Bring up Shemu’ĕl for me.”
28.12: And when the woman saw Shemu’ĕl, she cried out with a loud voice. And the woman spoke to Sha’ul, saying, “Why have you deceived me? You yourself are Sha’ul!”
28.13: And the meleḵ said to her, “Do not be afraid. What did you see?” And the woman said to Sha’ul, “I saw a mighty one coming up out of the earth.”
28.14: And he said to her, “What is his form?” And she said, “An old man is coming up, and he is covered with a mantle.” And Sha’ul knew that it was Shemu’ĕl, and he bowed with his face to the ground and did obeisance.
28.15: And Shemu’ĕl said to Sha’ul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” And Sha’ul answered, “I am deeply distressed, for the Pelishtites are fighting against me, and Elohim has turned aside from me and does not answer me anymore, neither by neḇi’im nor by dreams. So I have called you, to reveal to me what I should do.
28.16: Then Shemu’ĕl said, “And why do you ask me, seeing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has turned aside from you and has become your enemy?
28.17: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has done for Himself as He spoke by me. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has torn the reign out of your hand and given it to your neighbor, to Dawiḏ.
28.18: “Because you did not obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 nor execute His burning wrath upon Amalĕq, therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has done this matter to you today.
28.19: “Further, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 also gives Yisra’ĕl with you into the hand of the Pelishtites. And tomorrow you and your sons are with me. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 also gives the army of Yisra’ĕl into the hand of the Pelishtites.”
28.20: And immediately Sha’ul fell on the ground, his complete length, and greatly feared because of the words of Shemu’ĕl. And there was no strength in him, for he had eaten no food all day or all night.
28.21: And the woman came to Sha’ul and saw that he had been greatly disturbed, and said to him, “See, your female servant has obeyed your voice, and I have put my life in my hands and have listened to the words which you spoke to me.
28.22: “And now, please listen to the voice of your female servant too, and let me put a piece of bread before you. And eat, so that you have strength when you go on your way.”
28.23: But he refused and said, “I am not going to eat.” But his servants, together with the woman, urged him. And he listened to their voice. So he rose from the ground and sat on the bed.
28.24: And the woman had a fatted calf in the house, and she quickly slaughtered it. And she took flour and kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread from it.
28.25: And she brought it before Sha’ul and his servants. And they ate, and rose up and went away that night.

29.1: And the Pelishtites gathered all their armies at Aphĕq, while Yisra’ĕl encamped by a fountain which is in Yizre’ĕl.
29.2: And the princes of the Pelishtites were passing on by hundreds and by thousands, and Dawiḏ and his men were passing on in the rear with Aḵish.
29.3: And the princes of the Pelishtites said, “Who are these Iḇrim?” And Aḵish said to the princes of the Pelishtites, “Is this not Dawiḏ, the servant of Sha’ul meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, who has been with me these days, or these years? And to this day I have found naught in him since he came over.”
29.4: But the princes of the Pelishtites were wroth with him, and the princes of the Pelishtites said to him, “Send the man back, let him return to the place which you have appointed for him, and do not let him go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he become our adversary. For with what could he appease his master, if not with the heads of these men?
29.5: “Is this not Dawiḏ, of whom they sang to each other in dances, saying, ‘Sha’ul smote his thousands, and Dawiḏ his ten thousands’?”
29.6: And Aḵish called Dawiḏ and said to him, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, you have been straight, and your going out and your coming in with me in the army is good in my eyes. For to this day I have not found evil in you since the day of your coming to me. But in the eyes of the princes you are not good.
29.7: “And now, return, and go in peace, and do no evil in the eyes of the princes of the Pelishtites.”
29.8: And Dawiḏ said to Aḵish, “But what have I done? And to this day what have you found in your servant as long as I have been with you, that I should not go and fight against the enemies of my master the meleḵ?”
29.9: But Aḵish answered and said to Dawiḏ, “I know that you are as good in my eyes as a messenger of Elohim, but the princes of the Pelishtites have said, ‘Let him not go up with us to the battle.’
29.10: “And now, rise early in the morning with your master’s servants who have come with you. And as soon as you are up early in the morning and have light, then go.”
29.11: And Dawiḏ and his men rose up early to go in the morning, to return to the land of the Pelishtites, and the Pelishtites went up to Yizre’ĕl.

3.1: And the young Shemu’ĕl was serving 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 before Ĕli. And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was rare in those days - no vision breaking forth.
3.2: And it came to be in that day, that Ĕli was lying down in his place. And his eyes had begun to grow so dim that he was unable to see,
3.3: and the lamp of Elohim had not gone out in the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 where the ark of Elohim was, and Shemu’ĕl was lying down to sleep.
3.4: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 called Shemu’ĕl, and he answered, “Here I am!”
3.5: He then ran to Ĕli and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” But he said, “I did not call - lie down again.” So he went and lay down.
3.6: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 again called, “Shemu’ĕl!” And Shemu’ĕl arose and went to Ĕli, and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” But he answered, “My son, I did not call - lie down again.”
3.7: Now Shemu’ĕl did not yet know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was not yet revealed to him.
3.8: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 called Shemu’ĕl again the third time, and he arose and went to Ĕli, and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” Then Ĕli understood that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had called the youth.
3.9: So Ĕli said to Shemu’ĕl, “Go, lie down. And it shall be, if He calls you, say, ‘Speak, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for Your servant hears.’ ” And Shemu’ĕl went and lay down in his place.
3.10: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came and stood and called as at other times, “Shemu’ĕl! Shemu’ĕl!” And Shemu’ĕl answered, “Speak, for Your servant hears.”
3.11: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Shemu’ĕl, “See, I am doing a matter in Yisra’ĕl at which both ears of everyone who hears it shall tingle.
3.12: “In that day I shall confirm against Ĕli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from beginning to end.
3.13: “For I have declared to him that I am judging his house forever for the wickedness which he knows, because his sons brought a curse on themselves, and he did not rebuke them.
3.14: “And therefore I have sworn to the house of Ĕli that the wickedness of the house of Ĕli shall never be atoned for, by slaughtering or grain offering.”
3.15: And Shemu’ĕl lay down until morning, and opened the doors of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And Shemu’ĕl was afraid to report the vision to Ĕli.
3.16: Then Ĕli called Shemu’ĕl and said, “Shemu’ĕl, my son!” And he answered, “Here I am.”
3.17: And he said, “What is the word that He spoke to you? Please do not hide it from me. Elohim do so to you, and more also, if you hide a word from me of all the words that He spoke to you.”
3.18: And Shemu’ĕl reported to him all the words, and hid none from him. And he said, “It is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Let Him do what is good in His eyes.”
3.19: And Shemu’ĕl grew up, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was with him and did not let any of his words fall to the ground.
3.20: And all Yisra’ĕl from Dan to Be’ĕrsheḇa knew that Shemu’ĕl had been established as a naḇi of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.21: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 continued to appear in Shiloh, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 revealed Himself to Shemu’ĕl in Shiloh by the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

30.1: And it came to be, when Dawiḏ and his men came to Tsiqlaḡ, on the third day, that the Amalĕqites had invaded the South and Tsiqlaḡ, and smote Tsiqlaḡ and burned it with fire.
30.2: And they took captive the women and those who were there, from small to great. They did not kill anyone, but they led them away and went their way.
30.3: And Dawiḏ and his men came to the city and saw it burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.
30.4: And Dawiḏ and the people who were with him lifted up their voices and wept, until they had no more power to weep.
30.5: And Dawiḏ’s two wives, Aḥino’am the Yizre’ĕlitess, and Aḇiḡayil the widow of Naḇal the Karmelite, had been taken captive.
30.6: And Dawiḏ was greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the being of all the people was grieved, each for his sons and his daughters. But Dawiḏ strengthened himself in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim.
30.7: And Dawiḏ said to Eḇyathar the kohĕn, son of Aḥimeleḵ, “Please bring the shoulder garment here to me.” So Eḇyathar brought the shoulder garment to Dawiḏ.
30.8: And Dawiḏ inquired of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, “Do I pursue this band? Do I overtake them?” And He answered him, “Pursue, for you shall certainly overtake them, and certainly rescue.”
30.9: So Dawiḏ went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and came to the wadi Besor, where a halt was made by those who were left behind,
30.10: while Dawiḏ pursued, he and four hundred men - for two hundred halted, who were too faint to pass over the wadi Besor.
30.11: And they found a man in the field, a Mitsrite, and took him to Dawiḏ. And they gave him bread and he ate, and they let him drink water,
30.12: and gave him a piece of a cake of figs and two clusters of raisins. And when he had eaten, his strength came back to him, for he had not eaten bread nor drunk water for three days and three nights.
30.13: And Dawiḏ said to him, “To whom do you belong, and where are you from?” And he said, “I am a young man from Mitsrayim, servant of an Amalĕqite. And my master left me behind, for I had been sick three days.
30.14: “We attacked the south of the Kerĕthites and against that which belongs to Yahuḏah, and upon the south of Kalĕḇ, and we burned Tsiqlaḡ with fire.”
30.15: And Dawiḏ said to him, “Could you bring me down to this marauding band?” And he said, “Swear to me by Elohim that you neither kill me nor surrender me into the hands of my master, then I bring you down to this marauding band.”
30.16: And he brought him down and saw they were spread out over all the land, eating and drinking and dancing, because of all the great spoil which they had taken from the land of the Pelishtites and from the land of Yahuḏah.
30.17: And Dawiḏ smote them from twilight until the evening of the next day. And none of them escaped, except four hundred young men who rode on camels and fled.
30.18: And Dawiḏ rescued all that the Amalĕqites had taken. Dawiḏ also rescued his two wives.
30.19: And there was none missing of them, whether small or great, whether sons or daughters, or spoil or whatever they had taken from them. Dawiḏ recovered all.
30.20: Besides, Dawiḏ captured all the flocks and herds they had driven before those livestock, and they said, “This is Dawiḏ’s spoil.”
30.21: And Dawiḏ came to the two hundred men who were too faint to follow Dawiḏ, who had also been left at the wadi Besor. And they went out to meet Dawiḏ and to meet the people who were with him. And when Dawiḏ came near the people, he greeted them.
30.22: And all the evil and worthless men of those who went with Dawiḏ answered and said, “Because they did not go with us, we do not give them any of the spoil that we have rescued, except for every man’s wife and children, and let them take them and go.”
30.23: But Dawiḏ said, “My brothers, do not do so with what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given us, who has protected us and gave into our hand the band that came against us.
30.24: “And who would listen to you in this matter? For as his portion is who goes down to the battle, so is his portion who remains with the baggage, they share alike.”
30.25: And it came to be, from that day forward, he appointed it for a law and a right-ruling for Yisra’ĕl to this day.
30.26: And when Dawiḏ came to Tsiqlaḡ, he sent some of the spoil to the elders of Yahuḏah, to his friends, saying, “Here is a present for you from the spoil of the enemies of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,”
30.27: to those in Bĕyth Ĕl, and to those in Ramoth of the South, and to those in Yattir,
30.28: and to those in Aro’ĕr, and to those in Siphmoth, and to those in Eshtemoa,
30.29: and to those in Raḵal, and to those in the cities of the Yeraḥme’ĕlites, and to those in the cities of the Qĕynites,
30.30: and to those in Ḥormah, and to those in Korashan, and to those in Athaḵ,
30.31: and to those in Ḥeḇron, and to all the places where Dawiḏ had gone up and down, he and his men.

31.1: And the Pelishtites were fighting against Yisra’ĕl, and the men of Yisra’ĕl fled from before the Pelishtites, and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
31.2: And the Pelishtites followed hard after Sha’ul and his sons. And the Pelishtites smote Yahonathan, and Aḇinaḏaḇ, and Malkishua, sons of Sha’ul.
31.3: And the battle went hard against Sha’ul, and the archers hit him, so that he was severely wounded by the archers.
31.4: And Sha’ul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and thrust me through and roll themselves on me.” But his armor-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. So Sha’ul took the sword and fell on it.
31.5: And when his armor-bearer saw that Sha’ul was dead, he also fell on his sword, and died with him.
31.6: Thus Sha’ul died, and three of his sons, and his armor-bearer, also all his men, together on that day.
31.7: And they saw - the men of Yisra’ĕl who were beyond the valley, and those who were beyond the Yardĕn - that the men of Yisra’ĕl had fled and that Sha’ul and his sons were dead. So they forsook the cities and fled, and the Pelishtites came and dwelt in them.
31.8: And the next day it came to be, when the Pelishtites came to strip the slain, that they found Sha’ul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
31.9: And they cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and sent word throughout the land of the Pelishtites, to announce it in the house of their idols and to the people.
31.10: And they placed his armor in the house of the Ashtaroth, and they fastened his body to the wall of Bĕyth Shan.
31.11: And the inhabitants of Yaḇĕsh Gil’aḏ heard what the Pelishtites had done to Sha’ul,
31.12: and all the brave men arose and went all night, and took the body of Sha’ul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Bĕyth Shan. And they came to Yaḇĕsh and burned them there.
31.13: And they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Yaḇĕsh, and fasted for seven days.

4.1: Thus the word of Shemu’ĕl was to all Yisra’ĕl. And Yisra’ĕl went out to battle against the Pelishtites, and encamped beside Eḇen ha’Ĕzer, while the Pelishtites encamped in Aphĕq.
4.2: And the Pelishtites put themselves in battle array against Yisra’ĕl. And when the battle spread, Yisra’ĕl was smitten by the Pelishtites, who killed about four thousand men of the army in the field.
4.3: And when the people came into the camp, the elders of Yisra’ĕl said, “Why has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 smitten us today before the Pelishtites? Let us bring the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from Shiloh to us, so that He comes into our midst and save us from the hand of our enemies.”
4.4: And the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, dwelling between the keruḇim. And the two sons of Ĕli, Ḥophni and Pineḥas, were there with the ark of the Covenant of Elohim.
4.5: And when the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came into the camp, all Yisra’ĕl shouted so loudly that the earth shook.
4.6: And when the Pelishtites heard the noise of the shout, they said, “What is the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Iḇrim?” And when they knew that the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had come into the camp,
4.7: the Pelishtites were afraid, for they said, “Elohim has come into the camp!” And they said, “Woe to us! For it has never been like this before.
4.8: “Woe to us! Who shall deliver us from the hand of these mighty Elohim? These are the Elohim who smote the Mitsrites with all the plagues in the wilderness.
4.9: “Be strong and be men, you Pelishtites, that you do not become servants of the Iḇrim, as they have been to you. Be men, and fight!”
4.10: And the Pelishtites fought, and Yisra’ĕl was smitten, and every man fled to his tent. And the slaughter was very great, and there fell of Yisra’ĕl thirty thousand foot soldiers.
4.11: And the ark of Elohim was captured, and the two sons of Ĕli died, Ḥophni and Pineḥas.
4.12: And a man of Binyamin ran from the battle line the same day, and came to Shiloh with his garments torn and dirt on his head.
4.13: And he came in and saw Ĕli, sitting on a seat by the wayside watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of Elohim. And the man came into the city and reported it, and all the city cried out.
4.14: And Ĕli heard the noise of the outcry and said, “What is the noise of this uproar?” And the man came hastily and informed Ĕli.
4.15: Now Ĕli was ninety-eight years old and his eyes were so dim that he was unable to see.
4.16: And the man said to Ĕli, “I am he who came from the battle. And I fled today from the battle line.” And he said, “What was the matter, my son?”
4.17: And the messenger answered and said, “Yisra’ĕl has fled before the Pelishtites, and there has been a great slaughter among the people. And your two sons have died, Ḥophni and Pineḥas, and the ark of Elohim has been captured.”
4.18: And it came to be, when he made mention of the ark of Elohim, that Ĕli fell off the seat backward by the side of the gate. And his neck was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he ruled Yisra’ĕl forty years.
4.19: And his daughter-in-law, Pineḥas’ wife, was pregnant, about to bear. And when she heard the news that the ark of Elohim was captured, and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth, because her pains came upon her.
4.20: And about the time of her death the women who stood by her said to her, “Do not fear, for you have borne a son.” But she did not answer, nor did she put her heart to it.
4.21: And she called the child Iḵaḇoḏ, saying, “The esteem has departed from Yisra’ĕl!” because the ark of Elohim was taken and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
4.22: And she said, “The esteem has departed from Yisra’ĕl, for the ark of Elohim was taken.”

5.1: And the Pelishtites took the ark of Elohim and brought it from Eḇen ha’Ĕzer to Ashdoḏ,
5.2: and the Pelishtites took the ark of Elohim and brought it into the house of Daḡon and put it by Daḡon.
5.3: And the Ashdoḏites rose early in the morning and saw Daḡon fallen on its face to the ground before the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. So they took Daḡon and put it in its place again.
5.4: And they arose early the next morning and saw Daḡon fallen on its face to the ground before the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the head of Daḡon and both the palms of its hands cut off, on the threshold, only Daḡon itself was left of it.
5.5: That is why, to this day, the priests of Daḡon and all who come into Daḡon’s house do not tread on the threshold of Daḡon in Ashdoḏ.
5.6: But the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was heavy on the Ashdoḏites, and He wasted them and smote them with tumors - Ashdoḏ and its borders.
5.7: And when the men of Ashdoḏ saw this, they said, “Let not the ark of the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl remain with us, for His hand has been hard on us, and on Daḡon our mighty one.”
5.8: Then they sent and gathered to them all the princes of the Pelishtites, and said, “What do we do with the ark of the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl?” And they answered, “Let the ark of the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl be removed to Gath.” And they removed the ark of the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl .
5.9: And it came to be, after they removed it, that the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was against the city with a very great destruction. And He smote the men of the city, from the least to the greatest, and tumors broke out on them.
5.10: They then sent the ark of Elohim to Eqron. And it came to be, as the ark of Elohim came to Eqron, that the Eqronites cried out, saying, “They have removed the ark of the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl to us, to kill us and our people!”
5.11: And they sent and gathered together all the princes of the Pelishtites, and said, “Send away the ark of the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, and let it return to its own place, so that it does not kill us and our people.” For there had come a deadly destruction throughout all the city - the hand of Elohim was very heavy there.
5.12: And the men who did not die were smitten with tumors, and the cry of the city went up to the shamayim.

6.1: And the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was in the field of the Pelishtites for seven months.
6.2: And the Pelishtites called for the priests and the diviners, saying, “What do we do with the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄? Let us know with what we should send it to its place.”
6.3: And they said, “If you send away the ark of the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, do not send it empty, but you shall certainly return it to Him with a guilt offering. Then you are going to be healed, and it shall be known to you why His hand does not turn aside from you.”
6.4: And they said, “What is the guilt offering which we return to Him?” And they answered, “The number of the princes of the Pelishtites: five golden tumors and five golden rats. For the same plague was on all of you and on your princes.
6.5: “And you shall make images of your tumors and images of your rats that ruin the land, and you shall give esteem to the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl. It could be that He lifts His hand from you, from your mighty ones, and from your land.
6.6: “And why do you harden your hearts as the Mitsrites and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When He had severely dealt with them, did they not send them away, and they went?
6.7: “And now, take and make a new wagon, and two milk cows which have never been yoked, and hitch the cows to the wagon. And take their calves home, away from them.
6.8: “And take the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and put it on the wagon. And put the objects of gold which you are returning to Him as a guilt offering in a chest by its side, and send it away, and it shall go.
6.9: “And you shall see, if it goes up the way to its own border, to Bĕyth Shemesh, then He has done us this great evil. But if not, then we shall know that His hand has not come against us - an accident it was to us.”
6.10: And the men did so and took two milk cows and hitched them to the wagon, and shut up their calves at home.
6.11: And they put the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on the wagon, and the chest with the gold rats and the images of their tumors.
6.12: And the cows went straight for the way to Bĕyth Shemesh, and went along the highway, bellowing as they went, and did not turn aside, right or left. And the princes of the Pelishtites went after them to the border of Bĕyth Shemesh.
6.13: And Bĕyth Shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley. And they lifted their eyes and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it.
6.14: And the wagon came into the field of Yahoshua of Bĕyth Shemesh and stood there, and there was a great stone. So they split the wood of the wagon and offered the cows as a burnt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
6.15: And the Lĕwites took down the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the chest that was with it, in which were the objects of gold, and put them on the great stone. And the men of Bĕyth Shemesh slaughtered burnt offerings and made offerings the same day to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
6.16: And when the five princes of the Pelishtites saw it, they returned to Eqron the same day.
6.17: And these are the gold tumors which the Pelishtites returned as a guilt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄: one for Ashdoḏ, one for Azzah, one for Ashqelon, one for Gath, one for Eqron,
6.18: and the gold rats, by the number of all the cities of the Pelishtites belonging to the five princes, both walled cities and country villages, even as far as the great meadow on which they placed the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, are to this day in the field of Yahoshua of Bĕyth Shemesh.
6.19: And He smote among the men of Bĕyth Shemesh, for they had looked into the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. He smote among the people seventy men, and the people mourned because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 smote among the people, a great smiting.
6.20: And the men of Bĕyth Shemesh said, “Who is able to stand before this qodesh 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim? And to whom shall He go from us?”
6.21: And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Qiryath Ye’arim, saying, “The Pelishtites have brought back the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Come down, take it up to you.”

7.1: And the men of Qiryath Ye’arim came and took the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and brought it into the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ on the hill, and qadosh El’azar his son to guard the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
7.2: And it came to be, from the day that the ark remained in Qiryath Ye’arim, that the time increased, it came to be twenty years. And all the house of Yisra’ĕl lamented after 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
7.3: And Shemu’ĕl spoke to all the house of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “If you return to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with all your hearts, then put away the foreign mighty ones and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and serve Him only, so that He delivers you from the hand of the Pelishtites.”
7.4: And the children of Yisra’ĕl put away the Ba’als and Ashtaroth, and served 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 only.
7.5: And Shemu’ĕl said, “Gather all Yisra’ĕl to Mitspah and let me pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for you.”
7.6: And they gathered to Mitspah and drew water, and poured it out before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they fasted that day, and said there, “We have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” And Shemu’ĕl rightly ruled the children of Yisra’ĕl at Mitspah.
7.7: And when the Pelishtites heard that the children of Yisra’ĕl had gathered together at Mitspah, the princes of the Pelishtites went up against Yisra’ĕl. And the children of Yisra’ĕl heard of it, and were afraid of the Pelishtites.
7.8: And the children of Yisra’ĕl said to Shemu’ĕl, “Do not cease to cry out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim for us, that He would save us from the hand of the Pelishtites.”
7.9: And Shemu’ĕl took a suckling lamb and offered it as a burnt offering, completely, to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And Shemu’ĕl cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for Yisra’ĕl, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 answered him.
7.10: And it came to be, as Shemu’ĕl offered up the burnt offering, the Pelishtites drew near to battle against Yisra’ĕl. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 thundered with a great noise on that day on the Pelishtites, and troubled them, and they were smitten before Yisra’ĕl.
7.11: And the men of Yisra’ĕl went out from Mitspah and pursued the Pelishtites, and smote them as below Bĕyth Kar.
7.12: And Shemu’ĕl took a stone and put it up between Mitspah and Shĕn, and called its name Eḇen ha’Ĕzer, saying, “Thus far 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has helped us.”
7.13: Thus the Pelishtites were humbled, and no longer came into the border of Yisra’ĕl. And the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was against the Pelishtites all the days of Shemu’ĕl.
7.14: And the cities which the Pelishtites had taken from Yisra’ĕl were returned to Yisra’ĕl, from Eqron to Gath. And Yisra’ĕl recovered its border from the hands of the Pelishtites. And there was peace between Yisra’ĕl and the Amorites.
7.15: And Shemu’ĕl rightly ruled Yisra’ĕl all the days of his life,
7.16: and each year he made the rounds of Bĕyth Ĕl, and Gilgal, and Mitspah, and rightly ruled Yisra’ĕl in all those places.
7.17: Then he returned to Ramah, for his home was there. And there he rightly ruled Yisra’ĕl, and there he built an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

8.1: And it came to be, when Shemu’ĕl was old, that he made his sons rulers over Yisra’ĕl.
8.2: And the name of his first-born was Yo’ĕl, and the name of his second, Aḇiyah, rulers in Be’ĕrsheḇa.
8.3: But his sons did not walk in his ways, and turned aside after own gain, and took bribes, and twisted right-ruling.
8.4: And all the elders of Yisra’ĕl gathered together and came to Shemu’ĕl at Ramah,
8.5: and said to him, “Look, you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint for us a meleḵ to rule us like all the nations.”
8.6: But the word was evil in the eyes of Shemu’ĕl when they said, “Give us a meleḵ to rule us.” So Shemu’ĕl prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.7: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Shemu’ĕl, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you, for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me from reigning over them.
8.8: “According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Mitsrayim, even to this day - forsaking Me and serving other mighty ones - so they are doing to you too.
8.9: “And now, listen to their voice, but you shall certainly warn them, and shall make known to them the ruling of the meleḵ who reigns over them.”
8.10: And Shemu’ĕl spoke all the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to the people who asked him for a meleḵ,
8.11: and said, “This is the ruling of the meleḵ who reigns over you: He shall take your sons and appoint them for his own chariots and to be his horsemen, and they shall run before his chariots,
8.12: and appoint commanders over his thousands and commanders over his fifties, or to plough his ground and reap his harvest, or to make his weapons, and equipment for his chariots.
8.13: “And your daughters he is going to take to be perfumers, and cooks, and bakers.
8.14: “And the best of your fields, and your vineyards, and your olive trees he is going to take and give them to his servants.
8.15: “And a tenth of your grain and your vintage he is going to take and give it to his officers and servants.
8.16: “And your male servants and your female servants and your best young men and your donkeys he is going to take and use for his own work.
8.17: “A tenth of your sheep he is going to take, and you are to be his servants.
8.18: “And you shall cry out in that day because of your meleḵ whom you have chosen for yourselves, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is not going to answer you in that day.”
8.19: However, the people refused to listen to the voice of Shemu’ĕl, and said, “No, but let a meleḵ be over us.
8.20: Then we shall be, we also, like all the nations, and our meleḵ shall rule us and go out before us and fight our battles.”
8.21: And Shemu’ĕl heard all the words of the people, and he repeated them in the hearing of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.22: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Shemu’ĕl, “Listen to their voice, and make them a meleḵ.” And Shemu’ĕl said to the men of Yisra’ĕl, “Each of you go to his city.”

9.1: And there was a man of Binyamin whose name was Qish, son of Aḇi’ĕl, son of Tseror, son of Beḵorath, son of Aphiyaḥ, a Binyamite, a mighty man of power.
9.2: And he had a son whose name was Sha’ul, young and handsome. And there was not a more handsome man than he among the children of Yisra’ĕl, taller than any of the people by the shoulders and upwards.
9.3: And the donkeys of Qish, father of Sha’ul, were lost. And Qish said to his son Sha’ul, “Please take one of the servants with you, and arise, go seek the donkeys.”
9.4: And he passed through the mountains of Ephrayim and through the land of Shalishah, but they did not find them. Then they passed through the land of Sha’alim, but they were not. Then he passed through the land of the Binyamites, but they did not find them.
9.5: They came to the land of Tsuph, and Sha’ul said to his servant who was with him, “Come, let us turn back, lest my father forgets about the donkeys and become worried about us.”
9.6: And he said to him, “See, there is in this city a man of Elohim, and the man is esteemed. All that he says comes true, without fail. Now, let us go there. It could be that he shows us the way to go.”
9.7: And Sha’ul said to his servant, “But look, if we go, what do we bring the man? For the bread in our bags is all gone, and there is no present to bring to the man of Elohim. What do we have?”
9.8: And the servant answered Sha’ul again and said, “Look, I have here at hand one fourth of a sheqel of silver. And I shall give that to the man of Elohim, and he shall make known to us our way.”
9.9: Formerly, in Yisra’ĕl, when a man went to inquire of Elohim, he spoke thus, “Come, let us go to the seer,” for the naḇi of today was formerly called a seer.
9.10: And Sha’ul said to his servant, “Your word is good. Come, let us go.” And they went to the city where the man of Elohim was.
9.11: As they went up the hill to the city, they met some young women going out to draw water, and said to them, “Is the seer here?”
9.12: And they answered them and said, “He is. Look, ahead of you. Hurry now, for he came to this city today, for the people have an offering on the high place today.
9.13: “As you come into the city, you are going to find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. For the people do not eat until he comes, for he baraḵ the slaughtering, afterward they who are invited eat. And now, go up, for you should find him about this time.”
9.14: And they went up to the city. They were coming into the midst of the city, and saw Shemu’ĕl coming out toward them to go up to the high place.
9.15: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had revealed to Shemu’ĕl in his ear the day before Sha’ul came, saying,
9.16: “At this time tomorrow I shall send you a man from the land of Binyamin, and you shall anoint him leader over My people Yisra’ĕl, and he shall save My people from the hand of the Pelishtites. For I have seen My people, because their cry has come to me.”
9.17: And when Shemu’ĕl saw Sha’ul, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to him, “See, the man of whom I spoke to you. Let this one govern My people.”
9.18: And Sha’ul drew near to Shemu’ĕl in the gate, and said, “Please inform me, where is the house of the seer?”
9.19: And Shemu’ĕl answered Sha’ul and said, “I am the seer. Go up before me to the high place, for you shall eat with me today. And tomorrow I shall let you go and make known to you all that is in your heart.
9.20: “As for your donkeys that were lost three days ago, do not lay your heart on them, for they have been found. And on whom is all the desire of Yisra’ĕl? Is it not on you and on all your father’s house?”
9.21: And Sha’ul answered and said, “Am I not a Binyamite - of the smallest of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, and my clan the least of all the clans of the tribe of Binyamin? Why then do you speak like this to me?”
9.22: And Shemu’ĕl took Sha’ul and his servant and brought them into the hall, and gave to them a place at the head of those who were invited, and there were about thirty men.
9.23: And Shemu’ĕl said to the cook, “Bring the portion which I gave you, of which I told you to put it aside.”
9.24: And the cook brought out the thigh with its upper part and put it before Sha’ul. And Shemu’ĕl said, “See what was kept back. It was put aside for you. Eat, for it has been kept for you for this appointed time, saying, “I have invited the people.” And Sha’ul ate with Shemu’ĕl on that day.
9.25: And they came down from the high place into the city, and Shemu’ĕl spoke with Sha’ul on the roof.
9.26: And they rose early. And it came to be about the dawning of the day that Shemu’ĕl called to Sha’ul on the roof, saying, “Rise, so that I send you on your way.” And Sha’ul rose, and both of them went outside, he and Shemu’ĕl.
9.27: As they were walking toward the edge of the city, Shemu’ĕl said to Sha’ul, “Say to the servant to go on ahead of us.” And he went on. “But you stand here a moment, so that I let you hear the word of Elohim.”
